section_intro: ABOUT BASETEN
section_responsibilities:
The Field Productivity & Enablement Lead is responsible for making our sales motion clear, practical, and repeatable.
This person will help define how we sell at Baseten: how managers run the business, how reps qualify and advance deals, how sales works with FDE, product, marketing, and support, and how those expectations get turned into training and day-to-day habits.
This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who excels at both strategy and execution.
You'll shape the system, but you won't stop at slides or frameworks.
You'll build the playbooks, run the training, coach to the behaviors, and help managers ensure the process is followed consistently.
We're not looking for someone who wants to force-fit a single methodology onto the business.
We're looking for someone who is fluent in MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, and similar approaches, and can take the best ideas from each, adapt them to a technical sales motion, and build an approach that fits how Baseten actually sells.
You'll report to the Head of Enablement and Productivity.
Frontline managers and reps are your primary customers.
- Manage operating model.
Define the core rhythms for frontline managers, including 1:1s, forecast calls, pipeline reviews, deal reviews, and coaching cadences.
Create clear expectations for how managers inspect deals, coach reps, and drive consistency across the team.
- Sales process and stage design.
Partner with sales leadership and RevOps to define stages, exit criteria, qualification standards, and pipeline mechanics.
Help turn the sales process into something managers and reps can actually use, and make sure CRM and tooling reinforce the process instead of creating workarounds.
- Cross-functional engagement.
Clarify how sales engages FDE, solutions architects, product, marketing, and customer support.
Define the handoffs, decision points, and joint working models that help teams support customers without confusion or duplicated effort.
- Methodology, skills, and training.
Help codify the sales methodology and build the training behind it.
Deliver enablement sessions, coach managers and reps, and raise the quality of qualification, deal progression, and account planning over time.
- Behavior change and adoption.
Make the work stick.
Measure whether the process is being used, where managers or reps are getting stuck, and what needs to change to improve ramp time, pipeline quality, forecast accuracy, and win rates.
section_requirements:
You know what good sales execution looks like and can translate that into a system other people can follow.
You can move from diagnosing a broken forecast call, to redesigning a stage framework, to standing in front of a room and teaching managers how to run a better pipeline review.
You bring credibility with sales leaders, managers, and reps because you've seen how strong sales teams operate and you know how to make process useful instead of bureaucratic.
You are structured, practical, and comfortable driving change across functions.
Strong candidates may come from a mix of backgrounds such as:
- A former AE or sales leader who has carried a quota, managed teams, and later moved into enablement, strategy, or operations.
- A sales enablement or sales effectiveness leader with strong experience in methodology, manager training, and curriculum design.
- A RevOps or sales strategy professional with deep process rigor and a strong point of view on pipeline, qualification, and inspection.
- A management consulting or sales transformation background with experience building operating models and driving adoption in fast-growing teams.

section_intro: ABOUT BASETEN
section_responsibilities:
Baseten's GTM org is in hyper growth.
As it grows and matures, the needs of the GTM stack get more sophisticated with scale - and this team exists to stay ahead of those needs.
Our GTM Engineering team plays a critical role in building and maintaining the connective tissue across Baseten's GTM tools, processes, and user experience for the field.
The GTM tooling landscape is changing fast, and the teams that win are the ones that adapt and iterate the fastest.
This role exists to make sure Baseten is one of them.
You'll design, build, and ship AI-powered workflows that scale our GTM functions as a competitive advantage.
We want someone who can walk in, audit what we have, identify what we're missing, and start shipping fast.
You know when to reach for Clay and when to build something custom in Claude Code.
You think two to three steps ahead about how the thing you build today fits into the broader systems architecture tomorrow.
And you bring a point of view - on our stack, on what we should be building, and on where AI can do something low-code tooling simply can't.
- Ship AI-powered workflows for the field - build the agents and automations that give reps and managers real leverage, off-loading the manual and repetitive work.
Reach for AI where it does something low-code can't.
- Get insights in front of reps - turn Salesforce, warehouse, and usage data into the dashboards, scores, and alerts reps actually act on.

section_intro: ABOUT BASETEN
section_responsibilities:
We're looking for an IT Engineer to design the systems behind how people at Baseten get access, stay secure, and move through their time here.
This role builds the controls and automation that our IT Operations team runs every day across identity, client platforms, SaaS, and cloud access.
The goal is a corporate environment that's secure by default and easy to use: access that's right from day one, removed when it should be, and provable at any time.
- Strengthen our identity platform with strong authentication, clean access models, and least privilege as the default.
- Automate the workforce lifecycle so that joining, changing roles, and leaving Baseten are fast, consistent, and need little manual work.
- Build reliable pipelines for OS updates, patching, and software deployment that keep the fleet current without disrupting people's work.
- Connect device health to access decisions, so a compliant device is what earns access to sensitive systems.
- Recommend identity and security standards for our SaaS and AI tools, and make the secure configuration the easy path for teams adopting new ones.
- Bring governance to non-human identities (service accounts, API keys, AI agents) and replace long-lived credentials with better options wherever possible.
- Manage configuration as code across identity and endpoints to reduce drift, so audit readiness comes from the systems themselves instead of a separate workstream.
- Give IT Operations well-designed tools and guardrails, so they can handle more requests on their own, safely.
section_requirements:
- 5+ years in IT engineering or corporate security engineering, ideally at a cloud-native company.
- Strong grounding in identity: SSO, MFA, provisioning, and the protocols behind them.
- Hands-on experience engineering macOS fleets at scale: MDM, configuration profiles, app packaging and deployment, and endpoint visibility and EDR tooling.
- Experience automating real workflows in code (Python, Bash, or similar), and comfort with infrastructure-as-code.
- A working understanding of SaaS and cloud access risks, and how to reduce them without blocking the business.
- Good judgment about when to build, when to buy, and when to leave something alone.
- Clear writing, and a track record of working across IT, People, Engineering, Legal, GRC and Security.

section_intro:
ABOUT BASETEN
We are looking for an engineer with strong experience in machine learning and solid foundations in math and computer science to join our growing Post-Training team at Baseten.
section_responsibilities:
Custom models are instrumental to the success of Baseten customers.
By inference volume, the overwhelming majority of traffic at Baseten is to and from models that have been post-trained in some way, whether that be through reinforcement learning, supervised finetuning, a recent technique from the literature, or an in-house research technique from Baseten.
The Post-Training team is responsible for the success of our customers' post-trained models, and we employ a wide array of techniques to produce models that are more efficient and higher quality than even the biggest closed source models for the customer's specific needs.
Your role as a research engineer is to build the in-house tooling to support all of this.
We care about training a wide spectrum of different model architectures with a variety of techniques efficiently and at scale.
At times this involves zooming deep into a particular technical topic, but more often it involves working across the stack as a whole - systems-level concepts like Kubernetes, cgroups, storage systems, and networking topologies, as well as PyTorch distributed tensor computation, and GPU kernels.
The Manifesto:
RECENT RESEARCH
- Dense, on-policy or both?
- Repeated kv cache for long-running agents
- Distillation without the dark - replicating black-box on-policy distillation on Baseten
We don't have a rigid set of skills, but here's some of what we're looking for:
- A deep understanding of modern ML techniques and tools for training transformers
- Advanced experience in a tensor/array computation library like PyTorch, TensorFlow, Jax, or similar
- A detailed understanding of transformer training parallelism strategies like data parallelism, sharded data parallelism, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, context parallelism
- The experience and knowledge to profile and improve the performance of a distributed GPU program in PyTorch or a similar library
- The ability to perform roofline analysis on a transformer training setup
- A willingness to dive into messy problems, work with researchers, derive specifications by asking important questions, and execute
- Familiarity with HPC and distributed computing platforms like Slurm, Ray, Kubernetes, and Dask
- Familiarity with cluster networking technology like Infiniband, RoCE, GPUDirect
- Solid fundamentals in operating systems concepts like processes, files, kernel drivers, containerization, and networking protocols
- A sense of creativity and willingness to ask difficult questions about our approach, assumptions, and tooling choices

section_intro: ABOUT BASETEN
section_responsibilities:
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead part of our Inference Performance team.
This team makes the world's most demanding AI workloads run faster and more efficiently on GPUs.
You'll manage and grow a team of inference performance engineers working across the inference engine and runtime: kernels, scheduling, batching, KV-cache management, speculative decoding and prefill/decode disaggregation.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role.
You'll set direction, unblock hard problems and earn the team's trust by going deep on GPU performance, while also hiring, developing and supporting the people doing the work.
Your team's output directly affects how fast our customers' models run and how efficiently we serve them.
The team is scaling quickly, so you'll help shape how it is structured as it grows.
EXAMPLE INITIATIVES
Your team will work on these types of projects as part of our Inference Runtime team:
- Agentic inference optimization: 50-90% faster engines
- Agentic Kernels in Production
- Live draft model training for speculative decoding
- The Baseten Inference Stack
- Lead, mentor and grow a team of inference performance engineers through regular 1:1s, clear feedback, career development and performance reviews.
- Hire top GPU and inference engineering talent, and build a strong, collaborative team culture as the runtime team scales.
- Own the technical roadmap and execution for runtime performance work, balancing customer needs, new model launches and long-term platform investments.
- Stay close to the technical work.
Review designs, guide profiling and optimization efforts, and help the team reason from first principles about where time and memory go.
- Drive the productionization of inference techniques such as quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, chunked prefill and custom scheduling.
- Turn performance wins into measurable outcomes: tokens per GPU-hour, utilization, latency and cost.
- Help the team bring up and tune new model architectures on new hardware quickly, often in the same week they're released.
- Partner with Infrastructure, Inference Platform, Kernels, Model APIs and customer-facing teams to set priorities, coordinate launches and ship wins.
- Set high standards for engineering quality, benchmarking, operational excellence and incident response.
section_requirements:
- Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
- Experience managing engineers, including hiring, mentoring, giving feedback and running performance reviews.
- Experience leading or closely supporting GPU optimization teams in training, inference or recommendation systems.
- Strong technical depth in GPU workloads, with a solid understanding of GPU architecture and performance tradeoffs.
- Familiarity with ML libraries such as PyTorch, TensorRT or TensorRT-LLM.
- A track record of driving roadmaps and shipping complex technical projects with a team.
- Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to align stakeholders across teams.
section_preferred:
- Familiarity with inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM.
- Experience with LLM optimization techniques (e.g., quantization, speculative decoding, continuous batching) in production.
- Experience with GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar).
- Experience scaling a team through rapid growth at a startup.
- A background as a hands-on performance or systems engineer before moving into management.

You'll make a meaningful impact on people's daily lives and help reshape these industries.

- How Notion achieved 2-3x lower latency with AI Meeting Notes
- Cost-efficient, high-performance TTS with Qwen3-TTS
- Fine-tuning Qwen3-TTS for high-quality voice cloning
- The fastest Whisper - with streaming and diarization
- NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Diarization: real-time speaker labels at a cent per audio hour
- Own and lead Voice AI product areas end-to-end - from architecture and system design through implementation, rollout, and long-term production operations.
- Design, build, and operate real-time, large-scale, high-performance model serving systems for STT, TTS, and voice agent workloads for mission-critical customer deployments
- Drive cross-team collaboration with sister engineering teams to solve full-stack technical problems, align on priorities, and coordinate end-to-end delivery across the product surface area
- Mentor teammates through code reviews, design docs, and technical leadership.

We're hiring Software Engineers with strong product and customer sense to join our Product Platform organization.
This team builds the enterprise-hardened products that sit on top of our inference platform.
These are the surfaces customers, partners, and their agents touch every day.
We also build systems and products for developer productivity, including agentic platforms.

- Commercialization, billing, and partnerships.
- Developer productivity and agentic development.
- Enterprise controls: identity, access, governance, and account lifecycle management.

Baseten is seeking talented and experienced Software Engineers to join our Platform team within the Infrastructure organization.
As a member of Baseten's Platform Team, you will own the systems that let every engineer at Baseten prove their code works before it reaches production.
Our product runs mission-critical AI inference for customers who measure downtime in dollars per second, which means our internal bar for correctness, performance, and failure tolerance has to be exceptional.
Your focus is the full testing stack: fast and reliable unit test tooling, integration harnesses that spin up realistic environments on demand, load and performance testing for GPU-backed inference workloads, and resilience testing that deliberately breaks things so our customers never have to find out what happens when a node dies mid-request.
This is a builder role with org-wide leverage.
You won't be writing tests for other teams - you'll be building the frameworks, harnesses, and feedback loops that make writing good tests the path of least resistance, and you'll set the standards for what "well-tested" means at Baseten.
- Own Baseten's testing strategy end to end - define the standards, the tiers, and the tooling that engineering teams build against.
- Build and maintain unit, integration, load and performance testing frameworks
- Design end to end test infrastructure that provisions realistic dependencies on demand - ephemeral Kubernetes namespaces, containerized service dependencies, etc.
- Build resilience and chaos testing capabilities: fault injection, network partition and latency simulation, pod and node failure scenarios, dependency degradation, and automated verification that our systems degrade gracefully and recover.
- Attack test suite reliability head-on - flake detection and quarantine, test impact analysis and selective execution, parallelization, and aggressive reduction of end-to-end CI wall time.
- Build observability into the testing layer itself: coverage reporting, test health dashboards, failure triage tooling, and clear signals about which areas of the codebase are under-tested.
- Create project templates and shared libraries so new services start with a complete testing setup on day one.
- Partner directly with product and infrastructure teams - embed where needed, understand their hardest testing problems, and turn one-off solutions into platform capabilities.
- Mentor engineers across the org on testing practice and raise the collective bar through code review, documentation, and internal advocacy.

- Deep experience with testing frameworks and their internals - pytest, Go's testing package, testify, testcontainers, or equivalents - including the ability to extend them, not just use them.
- Experience designing integration test infrastructure for distributed systems, including ephemeral environment provisioning and dependency management.
- Practical experience with load and performance testing tools (k6, Locust, Vegeta, JMeter, Gatling, or similar) and the judgment to interpret results and drive action from them.
- Solid Kubernetes and Docker fundamentals - you can build test infrastructure that runs on and tests against real cluster environments.
- Advanced understanding of CI/CD, including how to keep large test suites fast, deterministic, and trustworthy at scale.
- A track record of measurably improving testing culture on an engineering team - you have opinions on what to test, what not to test, and where the ROI actually is.

section_intro: ABOUT BASETEN
section_responsibilities:
Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes gets its own microVM, where it writes and runs code, calls tools, and keeps state across long tasks.
Agents pause and resume constantly, so the machine underneath has to start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume fast, and keep every tenant isolated while it does.
General-purpose virtualization was not built for that workload.
The Agent Infra team builds that layer.
Sandboxes run in microVMs with custom Linux kernels on bare-metal servers we operate.
You'll own how sandboxes start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume, and how they perform on each host's CPU and memory, down to the hardware.
You'll also own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to different storage classes for performance or capabilities, and the virtual devices that connect it securely to the network.
In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel whose microVM sandboxes are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes
We are building a cloud, not just using one.
That means designing for many tenants from day one and thinking through what each decision means all the way down to the datacenter.
The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.
If you've worked deep in KVM and Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or QEMU and want to build the computers AI agents run on, we'd love to talk.
EXAMPLE INITIATIVES
- Blaxel is joining Baseten to build the future of agentic infrastructure
- Securing the open frontier with NVIDIA OpenShell and Blaxel sandboxes
- Baseten Sandboxes documentation
- Own the microVM lifecycle for agent sandboxes: start, stop, suspend, resume, snapshot, and fork
- Build and tune the custom guest kernels sandboxes run on
- Tune host CPU and memory configuration so sandboxes run fast and safely on each type of hardware we operate
- Manage host-level resources and sandbox density on each machine
- Own startup and resume performance end to end, from VM boot or snapshot restore to the first command
- Own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to storage, and the virtual devices that connect it to the network
- Design isolation for multi-tenant workloads where the hypervisor is the security boundary
- Debug virtualization and isolation issues at scale, from userspace through the kernel to the hardware
- Contribute architecture decisions and code back to the open-source projects we build on

- Hands-on experience with KVM, plus Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or QEMU
- Deep understanding of Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, memory management, and the boot path
- Experience building cloud infrastructure as the provider (multi-tenant compute that customers run on), not only running workloads on a cloud provider
- Experience building multi-tenant infrastructure where isolation is a security boundary
- Strong systems programming background in Rust and/or Go; C/C++ also welcome
- Experience debugging performance and correctness problems across userspace and kernel boundaries
- You move fast and like owning a problem end to end on a small team

job_title: Technical Program Manager, AI Delivery for Public Sector & Defence, Canada
section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Why This Role?
We're seeking an experienced Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Program Management team, with a focus on Canadian public sector and defence accounts.
This is a highly specialized role requiring an individual who understands technical program delivery, the technical complexity of frontier AI models and the unique requirements of government and defence organizations.
You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of Canadian federal departments, provincial agencies, Crown corporations, and defence organizations.
You'll navigate complex procurement processes, stringent security requirements, data sovereignty concerns, and regulatory compliance while ensuring our customers successfully deploy and scale our AI solutions.
In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the technical program lead and trusted advisor for our most sensitive and high-impact government engagements.
Location: Ottawa required
Security Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance strongly preferred; candidates eligible and willing to obtain clearance will also be considered.
section_about:
This isn't typical program management-it's a highly specialized role at the intersection of frontier AI, national security, and public sector digital transformation.
You'll work on some of Canada's most sensitive and impactful AI deployments, helping government organizations harness cutting-edge technology while maintaining the highest standards of security, ethics, and accountability.
If you're passionate about responsible AI adoption, understand the unique constraints and opportunities within government, and want to have an outsized impact on how Canada leverages AI to serve its citizens, this role is for you.
HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:
section_responsibilities:
Customer Program Leadership:
- Own end-to-end technical program delivery for Canadian public sector and defence customers, from initial deployment through production scaling
- Serve as the primary technical program point of contact for government customers, building trusted relationships with departmental CIOs, IT directors, and technical teams
- Translate complex government requirements (security, compliance, accessibility, bilingualism, data sovereignty) into actionable engineering plans
- Navigate government procurement processes, RFP responses, and contractual technical obligations.
Strategic Communication:
- Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across Cohere's engineering organization, customer stakeholders, and government leadership
- Translate between AI/ML technical concepts and government-appropriate language for decision-makers who may not have deep technical backgrounds
- Present technical roadmaps and status updates to senior government officials and departmental executives
- Represent Cohere's technical capabilities in sensitive government and defence contexts.
Complex Program Management:
- Create and manage project schedules that account for government timelines, security review processes, and ministerial approval cycles
- Identify and manage dependencies across government departments, security authorities, cloud service providers, and internal Cohere teams
- Navigate risks unique to government deployments: privacy compliance, Algorithmic Impact Assessments, Treasury Board submissions, security authorizations
- Drive alignment between product development priorities and specific government requirements.
Technical Delivery & Execution:
- Ensure on-time delivery of AI solutions that meet government-grade security, privacy, accessibility, and performance standards
- Coordinate technical work across multiple teams: model customization, security hardening, integration with government systems, bilingual support
- Establish governance checkpoints appropriate for high-stakes government deployments
- Problem-solve complex technical challenges in air-gapped, on-premises, or highly regulated environments.
You May Be a Good Fit If:
Required Experience:
- 6+ years of experience as a customer-facing Technical or Engineering Program Manager in AI/ML consulting, technology transformation, or enterprise software delivery.
- Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management.
- Experience working with government, defence, or heavily regulated customers (public sector, defence contractors).
- Proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs with stringent compliance requirements.
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field; advanced degree or technical certs a plus.
Technical Background:
- Strong understanding of enterprise software deployment architectures (cloud, on-premises, hybrid, air-gapped)
- Working knowledge of or experience with modern AI: LLMs, agentic systems, MCP, RAG, fine-tuning, evals, and responsible AI would be a strong differentiator
- Comfortable discussing API integrations, model inference, data pipelines, and ML operations with technical stakeholders.
Government & Defence Acumen:
- Deep understanding of how government organizations procure, evaluate, and deploy technology
- Familiarity with Canadian government requirements: data sovereignty, privacy laws (Privacy Act), accessibility standards, official languages obligations, security classifications
- Understanding of defence and national security considerations in AI deployment
- Experience with Algorithmic Impact Assessments or AI ethics frameworks is a strong asset
- Eligible to obtain Canadian government security clearance (Top Secret preferred)
section_preferred:
- Active Canadian government security clearance (Secret or Top Secret) - strong preference for active Top Secret clearance
- Bilingual (English/French) proficiency
- Background in or strong familiarity with Canadian defence, intelligence, or critical infrastructure sectors
- Experience with GC Cloud services (Azure, AWS GovCloud) or Protected B/C environments
- Project management certification (PMP, PgMP) or government-specific methodologies.
Security Clearance Requirements
This role requires eligibility for Canadian government security clearance.
Strong preference will be given to candidates who currently hold an active Top Secret (TS) clearance, as this will enable immediate engagement with our most sensitive defence and national security customers.
However, we will also consider exceptional candidates who:
- Currently hold Secret clearance and are eligible for TS upgrade
- Do not currently hold clearance, but are eligible and willing to undergo the Top Secret clearance process
- Have a previous government security clearance that has lapsed
Please note that obtaining Top Secret clearance can take 12-18 months.
Candidates without active clearance will work on non-classified public sector accounts while the clearance process is underway.

section_intro:
Who are we?
Our mission is to scale intelligence to serve humanity.
We're training and deploying frontier models for developers and enterprises who are building AI systems to power magical experiences like content generation, semantic search, RAG, and agents.
We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI.
We like to work hard and move fast to do what's best for our customers.
Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are passionate about their craft.
Each person is one of the best in the world at what they do.
We believe that a diverse range of perspectives is a requirement for building great products.
Join us on our mission and shape the future!
Why this role?
We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all.
Data quality is foundational to this process.
Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans: by way of feedback.
By labeling, ranking, auditing, prompting, red teaming, and correcting output, you will improve Large Language Model's performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere's tech.
Cohere is looking for Data Annotation Specialists with backgrounds and skills in Trust & Safety, Content Moderation, AI model evaluation, or related fields.
This role is best suited for candidates who bring strong contextual judgment, cultural and bias sensitivity, and experience applying nuanced guidelines to complex or ambiguous content.
Successful candidates will be highly detail-oriented, comfortable evaluating safety risks across different user intents and scenarios, and able to make consistent, well-reasoned decisions with a high degree of independence after onboarding.
IMPORTANT CONTEXT ON THIS ROLE: In this position, you will be asked to engage with human-generated and model-generated tasks which will sometimes mean intentional exposure to explicit content.
Your annotations on these explicit tasks will be used to prevent the Large Language Model from generating unintentional, adversarial, toxic, or unsafe outputs.
The types of explicit content you may be exposed to may include but are not limited to those of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.
Please Note: This is a part-time, remote, independent contractor position available within Canada or the United States.
We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 45 CAD/hour or 40 USD/hour contract rate, depending on your location, consisting of 30/hour base pay plus 15 CAD or 10 USD/hour hazard pay.
12 months contract with potential for extension.
As a Data Annotation Specialist on safety task, you will:
- Evaluate and improve model safety: Label, rank, audit, and refine human- and model-generated text to improve safety, quality, and policy alignment, including content that may be sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing.
- Apply nuanced safety judgment: Assess model outputs against detailed safety guidelines, rubrics, and style standards, making consistent decisions across ambiguous, sensitive, and context-dependent cases.
- Create prompts and safety test cases: Write realistic prompts, user scenarios, and adversarial examples that help evaluate model behavior across safety categories and uncover unsafe, evasive, over-refusing, or policy-inconsistent responses.
- Support quality and calibration: Identify annotation inconsistencies or unclear guidelines, and provide actionable feedback on recurring edge cases, model failures, and opportunities to improve data quality.
- Work with precision and independence: Complete annotation tasks with strong attention to detail, while being comfortable working independently in a globally distributed, asynchronous team environment.
section_requirements:
- 1+ years of experience in Content Moderation,Trust and Safety, AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, red teaming, and/or prompt engineering preferred.
- Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and sensitive content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment and the ability to recognize and manage personal bias.
- Emotional resilience: Comfort working with content that contains unsafe, explicit, and/or toxic content, including content of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.
- Excellent command of written English and the ability to clearly justify content evaluations, including why an output is safe, unsafe, high-quality or low-quality.
Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.
- Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.
The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test - This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!
Offer - Independent Contractor Agreement
As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project.
Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.
If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities.

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Why This Role?
We're seeking an experienced Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Program Management team, with a focus on UK public sector and defence accounts.
This is a highly specialised role requiring an individual who understands technical program delivery, the technical complexity of frontier AI models and the unique requirements of government and defence organisations.
You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of UK Government and defence organisations.
You'll navigate complex procurement processes, stringent security requirements, data sovereignty concerns, and regulatory compliance while ensuring our customers successfully deploy and scale our AI solutions.
In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the technical program lead and trusted advisor for our most sensitive and high-impact government engagements.
Location: UK
Security Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance preferred; candidates with Active Secret clearance or those who are eligible and willing to obtain clearance will also be considered.
section_about:

You'll work on some of the UK's most sensitive and impactful AI deployments, helping government organisations harness cutting-edge technology while maintaining the highest standards of security, ethics, and accountability.
If you're passionate about responsible AI adoption, understand the unique constraints and opportunities within government, and want to have an outsized impact on how the UK leverages AI to serve its citizens, this role is for you.
HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:
section_responsibilities:
Customer Program Leadership:
- Own end-to-end technical program delivery for UK public sector and defence customers, from initial deployment through production scaling
- Serve as the primary technical program point of contact for government customers, building trusted relationships with departmental CIOs, IT directors, and technical teams
- Translate complex government requirements (security, compliance, accessibility, bilingualism, data sovereignty) into actionable engineering plans
- Navigate government procurement processes, RFP responses, and contractual technical obligations.
Strategic Communication:
- Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across Cohere's engineering organisation, customer stakeholders, and government leadership
- Translate between AI/ML technical concepts and government-appropriate language for decision-makers who may not have deep technical backgrounds
- Present technical roadmaps and status updates to senior government officials and departmental executives
- Represent Cohere's technical capabilities in sensitive government and defence contexts.
Complex Program Management:
- Create and manage project schedules that account for government timelines, security review processes, and ministerial approval cycles
- Identify and manage dependencies across government departments, security authorities, cloud service providers, and internal Cohere teams
- Navigate risks unique to government deployments: privacy compliance, security authorisations, technical and infrastructure constraints
- Drive alignment between product development priorities and specific government requirements.
Technical Delivery & Execution:
- Ensure on-time delivery of AI solutions that meet government-grade security, privacy, accessibility, and performance standards
- Coordinate technical work across multiple teams: model customisation, security hardening, integration with government systems, bilingual support
- Establish governance checkpoints appropriate for high-stakes government deployments
- Problem-solve complex technical challenges in air-gapped, on-premises, or highly regulated environments.
You May Be a Good Fit If:
Required Experience:
- 6+ years of experience as a customer-facing Technical or Engineering Program Manager in AI/ML consulting, technology transformation, or enterprise software delivery.
- Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management.
- Experience working with government, defence, or heavily regulated customers (public sector, defence contractors).
- Proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs with stringent compliance requirements.
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field; advanced degree or technical certs a plus.
Technical Background:
- Strong understanding of enterprise software deployment architectures (cloud, on-premises, hybrid, air-gapped)
- Working knowledge of or experience with modern AI: LLMs, agentic systems, MCP, RAG, fine-tuning, evals, and responsible AI would be a strong differentiator
- Comfortable discussing API integrations, model inference, data pipelines, and ML operations with technical stakeholders.
Government & Defence Acumen:
- Deep understanding of how government organisations procure, evaluate, and deploy technology
- Familiarity with UK government requirements: data sovereignty, privacy laws (Privacy Act), accessibility standards, official languages obligations, security classifications
- Understanding of defence and national security considerations in AI deployment
- Experience with Algorithmic Impact Assessments or AI ethics frameworks is a strong asset
- Eligible to obtain UK government security clearance (Top Secret preferred)
section_preferred:
- Active UK government security clearance (Secret or Top Secret) - preference for active Top Secret clearance
- Background in or strong familiarity with UK defence, intelligence, or critical infrastructure sectors
- Experience with GC Cloud services (Azure, AWS GovCloud) or Protected B/C environments
- Project management certification (PMP, PgMP) or government-specific methodologies.
Security Clearance Requirements
This role requires eligibility for UK government security clearance.
Preference will be given to candidates who currently hold an active UK government Top Secret (TS) clearance, as this will enable immediate engagement with our most sensitive defence and national security customers.
However, we will also consider exceptional candidates who:
- Currently hold UK government Secret clearance and are eligible for TS upgrade
- Do not currently hold clearance, but are eligible and willing to undergo the Top Secret clearance process
- Have a previous government security clearance that has lapsed
Please note that obtaining Top Secret clearance can take 12-18 months.
Candidates without active clearance will work on non-classified public sector accounts while the clearance process is underway.

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
WHY THIS ROLE?
This role is for a highly experienced Back-End Software Engineer who wants to work on core systems that shape how the platform (Model Vault) operates.
You will help define the architecture of the platform where reliability, security, performance, and simplicity all matter, and where many of the problems do not have off-the-shelf solutions.
Model Vault is Cohere's inference platform for deploying and operating models securely at enterprise scale.
The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing.
We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world's most demanding enterprise workloads.
AS A SENIOR/STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:
- Evolve and scale the backend systems that power Model Vault, including authentication and authorization, deployment management, billing, metering, and customer lifecycle.
- Lead major architectural initiatives across identity, payments, usage systems, platform scalability, and other core product foundations.
- Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.
- Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.
- Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.
- Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.
- Drive projects end-to-end, from architecture and threat modeling through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration based on real customer workloads.
YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:
- You are a strong backend engineer with excellent fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, networking, operating systems, and security.
- You have strong programming fundamentals and experience building production systems in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, or similar.
You write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and make thoughtful tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and correctness.
- You have designed and operated production systems where correctness, availability, security, and performance mattered at significant scale.
- You can take ambiguous, high-impact technical problems, define the right architecture, and drive them through to reliable production systems.
- You have strong systems-design instincts and understand concepts such as concurrency, consistency, caching, queues, rate limiting, backpressure, failure domains, idempotency, and graceful degradation.
- You think deeply about security boundaries and understand authentication, authorization, identity, cryptography, secrets, tenant isolation, and how small implementation choices can create significant security risks.
- You are comfortable reasoning across backend services, APIs, databases, distributed systems, and the cloud infrastructure they run on.
- You are comfortable diving into unfamiliar codebases and debugging complex problems that cross service or system boundaries.
- You care about the details of production engineering, including instrumentation, capacity planning, migrations, backwards compatibility, incident response, and safe rollouts.
- You are comfortable challenging existing architecture and evolving foundational components when the system's needs change.
- You have a track record of taking technically difficult projects from an unclear starting point to systems that other engineers and customers depend on.

WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Why this role?
Adoption of AI is moving rapidly from pilots to production.
Enterprises across APAC are investing in generative-AI programs, creating a once-in-a-decade market inflection point.
At Cohere, we're committed to transforming the Japan enterprise landscape through strategic partnerships and innovative AI solutions.
As a Partner Development Manager for the Japan Enterprise Market, you'll be at the heart of our mission to empower businesses across the region with cutting-edge AI technologies.
This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic, cross-cultural environment and is passionate about driving growth through collaboration.
You'll work closely with leading enterprises, system integrators, and technology partners to co-create value, expand market reach, and deliver impactful AI solutions tailored to the unique needs of Japanese businesses.
Japan is a key strategic market for Cohere, and your work will directly contribute to our success in this region.
You'll have the opportunity to shape partnerships that drive digital transformation, foster innovation, and position Cohere as a leader in the Japan AI ecosystem.
If you're a strategic thinker, a relationship builder, and eager to make a meaningful impact in one of the world's most dynamic markets, this role is your chance to shape the future of AI in Japan.
As our Partner Development Manager - Japan, you will own the success of our partner relationships in Japan.
Key responsibilities include:
Partner Strategy & Execution
- Define and execute Cohere's partner-go-to-market plan for the Japan Enterprise Market, aligning with regional business objectives.
- Partner with the broader GTM team to identify and recruit high-impact partners across system integrators, distributors, resellers, ISVs, and cloud providers.
- Develop relationships with key stakeholders across the partner ecosystem to ensure success of the partnership.
Partner Onboarding & Enablement
- Lead partner onboarding, certification, and training programs to ensure partners are equipped to sell, deploy and manage Cohere's solutions effectively.
- Collaborate with enablement to scale partner enablement in Japan through sales and technical workshops, empowering them to deliver value to enterprise customers.
Pipeline Generation & Co-Selling
- Own joint pipeline generation by creating co-sell motions, solution plays, and strategic joint go-to market motions that align Cohere's capabilities with enterprise mission needs and procurement cycles.
- Collaborate with partners to identify and pursue high-value opportunities across key Japan segments
Business Planning & Performance Tracking
- Ensure partners are aligned with Cohere's strategic goals and performance metrics.
- Run joint business planning sessions and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with partners, tracking sourced and influenced ARR against targets.
Partner Advocacy & Feedback
- Serve as the voice of the partner within Cohere, relaying feedback to Product, Engineering, and Legal teams
- Work with Cohere's Public Policy teams to navigate Japanese government AI policies to advise partners on risk management and responsible AI best practices.
Thought Leadership & Evangelism
- Evangelize Cohere's vision and solutions at partner and industry events, positioning Cohere as a leader in responsible GenAI for the Japanese market.
- Build thought leadership through briefings, speaking engagements, and collaborative initiatives.
Why You'll Love This Role
This is a high-impact role where you'll shape the future of AI partnerships in Japan.
You'll work at the intersection of technology, business, and policy, driving growth while ensuring responsible AI adoption.
If you're passionate about building strategic alliances, driving innovation, and making a difference in one of the world's most dynamic markets, this is the role for you.
What We're Looking For
- Native-level Japanese and business-level English fluency
- 8+ years of experience in partner development, channel sales, or alliance management within the tech industry, preferably in AI or cloud solutions, with a track record of enterprise ARR contribution
- Deep understanding of the Japanese enterprise market and key industry verticals.
- Strong relationship-building and negotiation skills, with a track record of driving partner success.
- Ability to navigate complex regulatory and compliance landscapes, including AI ethics and government policies.
- Working understanding of AI (LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows)
- Experience working with major system integrators, global consultancies, and hyperscalers including joint GTM and co-sell motions.
Existing relationship with Fujitsu preferred.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to evangelize Cohere's vision to partners and industry stakeholders.
- Results-driven growth mindset and bias for action.
You thrive in a start-up-speed environment and enjoy building and scaling partner programs

Cohere is revolutionizing enterprise AI with North, an agentic AI platform designed to securely deploy AI agents and automations within organizations' infrastructure.

We are seeking an Agent Harness Product Manager to own the execution layer that makes North agents reliable, capable, and production-ready.

Agent Loop and Execution.
Own the core agent runtime: tool orchestration, parallel execution, sub-agent delegation, sandbox code execution, and failure recovery.

Own the feedback loop between North's harness and the Modeling Team.

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
section_responsibilities:
You'll lead marketing operations and analytics at Cohere.
That covers the team, the martech stack, how we measure marketing's contribution to pipeline, and the budget and pipeline numbers marketing plans against.
When leadership asks what marketing produced last quarter and what to fund next, the answer starts with your numbers.
The role reports to the VP of Brand.
You'll work most closely with the Marketing Chief of Staff and the heads of Growth and Demand and Product Marketing, and every week with Revenue Operations, Sales Operations & Finance.
Web operations is part of marketing but doesn't report to this role.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
THE TEAM
You'll manage the marketing operations, automation, and analytics and data operations staff, and hire where you find gaps.
Marketing is growing rapidly, so you'll also bring acquired companies' systems and data into our stack.
MEASUREMENT
The attribution methodology is yours, documented and signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance.
Each quarter you'll present marketing's pipeline contribution to the executive team and say what you'd change.
Your analysts do the same for the program teams in Growth and Demand, Events and Product Marketing, showing which campaigns and channels are paying back their spend.
SYSTEMS AND DATA
Marketo, Looker, GA4 and 6sense are yours end to end, along with the campaign and lead side of Salesforce.
That includes forms, nurture, lead lifecycle, scoring and routing.
Campaign data needs to be structured well enough that analysts don't need workarounds, and target-account data has to reconcile to the governed account list.
With Revenue Operations, you'll make sure the data behind marketing's pipeline numbers can't change without a record, so a bulk edit can't quietly rewrite marketing's results.
A/B testing on nurture and forms sits with you too, sized so the results can be read.
Over time we want fewer tools and fewer dashboards, with one governed source for each metric.
BUDGET AND PLANNING NUMBERS
You'll own the martech and operations budget and track budget and headcount across marketing.
You'll also build the pipeline and capacity models marketing plans against.
The Marketing Chief of Staff runs planning and the business reviews and leads the trade-off conversations with your numbers in hand.
Marketing and Sales need to count pipeline the same way, every time.
YOUR FIRST YEAR
In the first 90 days, you'll document the attribution methodology and get it signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance.
By then we should also have an inventory of every reporting surface, each with a named owner, and your order for fixing the data problems you inherit.
By three months, one governed executive dashboard has replaced the competing decks in business reviews, and rebuilt lead routing is in production.
By six months, target-account reporting reconciles to the governed list, and anyone on the team can reproduce quarterly attribution from the documented method, with change control on the data underneath it.
The stack is smaller than when you arrived, and some marketing workflows run on agents in production.
Annual planning runs on your budget, headcount and pipeline models.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
MUST HAVE
- 10+ years in marketing operations or marketing analytics in B2B or enterprise software, including at least one high-growth company.
- You've managed a marketing operations and analytics team and its martech budget, setting priorities across ops, automation and analytics specialists and hiring to fill gaps.
- Hands-on Marketo and Salesforce experience with lead lifecycle, campaign structure, routing and the sync between the two.
You've configured these systems yourself.
- You've owned a multi-touch attribution model end to end and defended its definitions to a CFO or executive team.
- SQL, and enough comfort in a governed BI layer like Looker to check a number yourself before you present it.
- You've run the data side of an account-based motion, including the hygiene that makes a target account list reportable.
- You've worked closely with Revenue Operations and Sales Operations without duplicating their work.
- Experience in enterprise, regulated or public-sector buying environments, including GDPR and CASL as they apply to lead handling.
- You already use AI and automation in your own team's work.
section_preferred:
- Enterprise AI, infrastructure or developer-platform marketing.
- You've built agentic or LLM-based workflows in GTM operations and measured what they saved.
- Product-led funnel instrumentation running alongside a sales-led pipeline.
- You've consolidated an inherited martech stack, or merged systems after an acquisition.
HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:
If any of the above doesn't line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

Join us!

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Role Overview:
As a Senior Research Engineer in our Safety team, you will play a key role in helping develop safer, more secure, and more reliable models.
Your primary focus will be on building tools to enable easy data synthesis, analysis, and management, for complex combinations of real and synthetic data that is used in both model training and evaluation.
You will own the cohesive vision of these tooling repositories.
You will work closely with a team of research scientists and engineers to create tooling that enables tighter experimentation cycles, better data coverage of the real world, and more scientific rigour.
You will have a lot of autonomy and need to be opinionated about what areas of the codebase need elegance and standards, and where that would be overengineering.
You will be given high level experimental problems that need to be solved with efficient pipelines, and design and implement the solutions.
Your data analysis will collaboratively feed into modelling decisions and experimentation.
This role combines expertise in software engineering, statistics, and data science.
If any of these topics sound interesting to you, we encourage you to apply.
You will be working on the Modelling Safety and Trust team, so interest in these areas is a plus, but is not at all required.
Please Note: We have offices in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Toronto, Montreal and New York, but we also embrace being remote-friendly!
This role has timezone restrictions (UK, Europe, or ET) but no location restrictions.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and implement robust data pipeline tooling that enables frequent, low-friction data generation and annotation
- Create cohesive data infrastructure that supports continuous parallel operation with model experimentation
- Establish standardized processes for data validation, analysis, and improvement of data both training and evaluation
- Collaborate with the ML modeling team to align data capabilities with experimental needs
- Maintain opinionated, well-documented solutions that become team standards
- Develop systematic analysis frameworks to identify incoming data sources and benchmark coverage gaps

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
section_about:
We are building a Government Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) team with the ambition and expertise to help shape one of the world's most dynamic environments for artificial intelligence and digital innovation.
As our Government Affairs Lead for the Middle East, you will help establish and strengthen Cohere's presence across the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the other Gulf Coast countries ensuring the company's voice contributes to the development of AI policy, digital transformation, public-sector innovation, procurement, and economic diversification initiatives.
This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced government affairs professional who thrives at the intersection of government, technology, and public policy, and who wants to help position Cohere as a trusted partner supporting the region's ambitions to become a global leader in artificial intelligence.
You will work alongside experienced policy leaders, collaborate closely with senior executives, and contribute directly to Cohere's strategic growth across two of the world's fastest-growing AI markets.
section_responsibilities:
- Report directly to Cohere's Head of EMEA Government Affairs & Public Policy, partnering closely with senior leadership, legal, public policy, responsible AI, communications, and commercial teams to develop and execute Cohere's government affairs and stakeholder engagement strategy across the UAE and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
- Serve as Cohere's primary government affairs representative across the region, building trusted relationships with ministries, regulators, government authorities, public-sector organizations, sovereign entities, and innovation agencies.
- Monitor and assess legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments affecting artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data governance, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure, and emerging technologies across the region.
- Support policy advocacy by developing consultation responses, policy submissions, briefing materials, executive talking points, and stakeholder engagement strategies related to AI regulation, digital economy initiatives, technology policy, and public procurement.
- Partner closely with commercial and public sector sales teams to support business development opportunities across government, financial services, telecommunications, energy, and other regulated industries.
- Collaborate with communications, marketing, and public relations teams to ensure consistent and effective messaging regarding Cohere's approach to responsible AI, innovation, and technology policy.
- Represent Cohere in industry associations, public-private partnerships, conferences, and policy forums across the Middle East.
- Develop and manage relationships with external government affairs consultants, advisors, and trade associations across the region.
- Ensure all government engagement, lobbying, and political activities are conducted in full compliance with applicable local laws, regulations, and company policies.
- Contribute to broader regional government affairs initiatives across the GCC and support cross-functional projects involving international stakeholders.
section_requirements:
- 7+ years of experience in government, a ministerial office, public policy, diplomacy, public-sector consulting, regulatory affairs, corporate government affairs, or a leading industry association.
- Strong understanding of the policymaking, regulatory, and public-sector landscape in either the United Arab Emirates or the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with the ability to quickly develop expertise across both markets.
- Experience building trusted relationships with senior government officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Familiarity with AI policy, digital transformation, innovation policy, cloud technologies, public procurement, or technology regulation.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex policy developments into clear business implications and actionable recommendations.
- A collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively across international, cross-functional teams spanning multiple time zones.
- An entrepreneurial, self-starter mentality with excellent stakeholder management and project execution skills.
- Passion for artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and the opportunity to help shape the policy environment supporting responsible AI adoption.
- An undergraduate degree in political science, international relations, public policy, law, business, economics, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
section_preferred:

- Existing relationships with government stakeholders in both the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
- Experience engaging with GCC institutions or regional organizations.
- Experience in enterprise software, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, or another emerging technology sector.
- Experience supporting government procurement, digital transformation, or national AI initiatives.

section_intro:
WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
WHY THIS ROLE?
We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it.
As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.
Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part.
A query that runs can still answer the wrong question.
Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model.
The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero.
Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.
You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt.
In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.
This is a hands-on staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics.
You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself.
You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.
section_responsibilities:
As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:
- Own the system end to end.
Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.
- Build and run it in production.
Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers.
Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability.
Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.
- Hold every release to the evaluation bar.
Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models.
Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.
- Engineer the context layer.
Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use.
Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.
- Roll it out across Cohere.
Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set.
Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.
- Make it replicable.
Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.
- Hire and lead the team.
Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.
- Partner across Cohere.
Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.
section_requirements:
- 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams
- Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail
- Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right
- Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO
- Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)
- Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar).
You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision
- Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail
- Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data
- Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds
- Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams
If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Why this role?
We're seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Engineering Program Management team.
We need someone with curiosity, drive, independence, and leadership, who has hands-on experience working directly with customers and managing projects for enterprise-grade software or enterprise-focused machine learning solutions.
In return, you'll have the unique opportunity to shape Cohere's operations, collaborate with leading minds in the LLM space, work directly with our Strategic Customers as well as Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform , Product and Go-to-Market teams, and be the "technical" voice of Cohere for the customer.
You will get a chance to create extremely high-impact contributions to our fast-growing company, product and culture.
As an Engineering Program Manager/ Technical Program Manager, you will:
- Communicate: Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across the tech organization, Cohere teams, leadership, and most importantly - our strategic customers and external partners.
- Optimize: Break down complex issues into strategies, driving engineering alignment with product, business, and marketing while fostering collaboration.
- Plan: Create and manage program/project schedules, identify dependencies, manage risks, and drive organizational alignment.
- Execute: Ensure on-time delivery, identify development needs, and establish checkpoints for status updates.
- Problem solve: Proactively identify and resolve issues, coordinate cross-functional dependencies, and prioritize impacts to schedule and product quality.
You may be a good fit if:
- You have at least 5 years of experience as an Engineering or Technical Program Manager, with at least 2 years in customer-facing technical delivery and operations focused on enterprise-grade AI software/solutions
- Knowledge or experience with LLM training or optimization would be a key differentiator
- You are problem-focused and making customers successful really excites you
- You are detail-oriented and extremely self-organized.
You love enabling people and teams around you, and are excellent at capturing detailed notes/action items during highly technical meetings and tracking progress.
- You have a Bias for Action - you are very execution focused and you like getting things done.
- You have experience working with cross-functional teams to get technical products, services or solutions shipped to an internal or an external customer and can independently own tracking and reporting across multiple work-streams, with owners in different time-zones.
- You are comfortable holding leaders and individual contributors accountable.
You can be assertive while remaining diplomatic.
You are not afraid to follow up with people to ensure shipping within committed deadlines.

WHO ARE WE?
Join us!
Why this role?
The Web team builds cohere.com the public face of Cohere.
We work with marketing, design, and leadership to ship polished pages quickly: landing experiences, content-driven UI, and the CMS systems behind them.
As a Web Developer, you will:
- Work closely with a small team of engineers, designers, and marketing partners
- Build and iterate on growth-focused UI: styling, layout, and content-driven pages
- Work with content editors so publishing is faster and less painful.
Better workflows, clearer schemas, fewer gotchas
- Ship experiments and marketing features that help people discover and try Cohere
- Build in Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind, including the Sanity schemas that power the site
- Improve performance and reliability where it actually moves the needle, not chase tech for its own sake
- Use AI coding tools every day, while owning what you merge: you should be able to debug, explain, and stand behind the code
You may be a good fit if:
- You've spent 2+ years shipping production React/TypeScript apps and care about polish and performance
- You're comfortable with Next.js and a headless CMS like Sanity or ready to ramp up quickly
- You like partnering with design and marketing, and you leave code a bit clearer than you found it
- You're excited to try new tools when they help, and skip them when they don't
- You care about the end result for users, not just the framework of the week
Bonus: Eye for design or motion; a portfolio, GitHub, or shipped marketing work.
Familiarity with monorepos (pnpm/Turborepo) or Vercel is a plus.
