section_intro: About Decagon
section_about:
Decagon's GTM Productivity team is laser-focused on building a truly elite, world-class revenue engine as a core differentiator for the business.
At the individual level, we believe in unlocking the full potential of every seller and field team member - enabling them to do their best work and win at the highest level.
At the organizational level, success means turning strategy into consistent, repeatable execution - driving faster ramp, higher productivity per rep, and exceeding global revenue targets with greater efficiency.
Decagon is looking for a Sales Enablement Manager - a founding member of our GTM Productivity team - to help our sellers and sales leaders win.
This is a highly tactical, field-facing role for someone who understands great selling firsthand, whether as a former seller or through experience in elite sales organizations.
You'll partner directly with sales leaders and their teams to coach sellers, improve execution, and drive measurable performance.
You'll be a trusted partner to the field in building programs, training, content, and certifications, to improve our sellers performance.
section_responsibilities:
- Partner directly with sales leaders and sellers - understanding day-to-day challenges, identifying performance gaps, and driving initiatives that help individuals and teams win.
- Build and deliver high-impact enablement - leading practical training, certifications, and ongoing development grounded in real customer conversations and deals.
- Drive a consistent field enablement cadence - facilitating engaging sessions alongside sales leaders and top performers to reinforce great selling behaviors.
- Partner cross-functionally - translating Product, Marketing, and business priorities into actionable field execution.
- Leverage data, tools, and AI - identifying coaching opportunities, measuring impact, and scaling effective enablement.
- 5+ years in B2B SaaS sales, sales leadership, or field enablement, ideally with firsthand quota-carrying experience or deep exposure to elite sales organizations.
- Strong sales acumen and credibility - you understand what great selling looks like and can translate that into practical coaching.
- Passion for developing sellers - you thrive on helping individuals and teams improve their performance.
- Exceptional communication and facilitation skills - equally comfortable coaching 1:1, leading workshops, and partnering with senior sales leaders.
- Scrappy, hands-on, and execution-oriented - you thrive in fast-moving environments and prioritize tangible business impact.
Even better if you have
- Experience transitioning from sales or sales leadership into enablement.
- Experience building sales coaching, training, or methodology programs.
- Experience in AI, enterprise SaaS, or high-growth startups.
- Experience leveraging AI and conversational intelligence to improve sales performance.

Decagon's Strategic Deals are with the largest companies in the world.
Each one puts a Decagon agent in front of millions of users, fielding hundreds of millions of conversations a year.
These deals are won on technical execution: hard problems without an off-the-shelf answer, latency and reliability constraints at real scale, and requirements that push the product into new territory.
You'll own the technical build for 1-3 Strategic Deals end-to-end, operating like the founding CTO of each.
You'll work directly with the customer's senior engineering and product leaders to figure out what they need for the deal to be successful.
From there, you decide what Decagon should build, ship it, and productionize it so it benefits every customer, not just this one.
You're across every technical workstream on the deal, from infrastructure and the agent build to model evaluation, research, and the reliability work that makes it production-grade.
You sit at the center of product strategy: your decisions shape not only each deployment, but also the feature set that gets reflected in the product itself.

section_intro: About Decagon
section_about:
Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it.
We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.
Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems.
The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents.
A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.
Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.
You'll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted.
That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.
You'll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch.
You'll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you're building is actually right for them.
On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes.
An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.
section_responsibilities:
- Build PII handling and redaction systems that identify and protect sensitive information across conversations, agent traces, and other customer data
- Design configuration abstractions for redaction and retention policies that balance enterprise flexibility with clear, safe defaults
- Build reliable data deletion workflows that propagate across storage systems and derived data, with retries, verification, and visibility into failures
- Build self-serve tools and APIs that let customers configure, test, and understand their data lifecycle policies without relying on an engineer
- Build LLM-backed systems that scan and detect data anomalies and violations
- Train and/or tune models for detecting data of various forms (including PII and PHI)
- Extend redaction and identification to multimodal agents, including images, attachments, voice notes, and documents.
- Build monitoring and auditability that make it clear what data was processed, what remains, and where a policy has failed-without exposing sensitive information in the process
- Handle data lifecycle systems at scale, including backfills, partial failures, and safe rollouts; your work will touch critical flows for Fortune 100 companies
- 4+ years building software products, with strong product thinking
- Proficient in Python, comfortable working across the entire stack
- Experience designing reliable backend systems and data pipelines, including asynchronous processing, retries, and failure recovery
- Understanding of what operational maturity looks like for critical systems, including observability and monitoring
- Complex systems instincts: you can reason about where data flows, where copies persist, and what happens when one part of a workflow fails
- A high degree of comfort debugging system failures in deep technology stacks, using whatever tool gets you to the answer
- Judgment about when to ship fast and when correctness, privacy, and irreversible operations require slowing down
Even better
- Experience with PII detection, redaction, tokenization, or secure handling of sensitive data
- Experience building data retention, deletion, or privacy request workflows across multiple storage systems
- Experience building security-sensitive product systems, such as authentication, authorization, and data access controls
- Familiarity with privacy and compliance requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, or PCI, and translating them into engineering controls
- Background with LLMs, evals, or AI agent systems, especially handling sensitive data in model inputs, outputs, and traces
- Experience with observability, audit trails, or operational tooling for large-scale data systems
- Work with sensitive data in voice, images, or other non-text formats

section_intro: About Decagon
section_about:
The AI Platform team builds the foundational systems that enable every engineer at Decagon to build with AI.
Our users are both engineers and coding agents.
We build the execution environments, agent harnesses, evaluation systems, developer tools, and shared abstractions they use to plan, write, test, review, and ship production software.
We sit within Infrastructure and work closely with product, ML, data, and security teams.
Our goal is to turn rapidly evolving agent capabilities into reliable, secure platforms that materially change how software gets built at Decagon.
We're looking for an experienced software engineer to help build Decagon's AI-native developer platform.
You'll work at the intersection of distributed systems, developer tooling, and applied AI.
You will experiment with new agentic workflows, identify where they create real leverage, and turn the best ideas into dependable systems used across the engineering organization.
This is a highly product-oriented platform role.
You'll work directly with engineers to understand how they build software, find high-value opportunities for automation, and own solutions from architecture and implementation through rollout, adoption, and production operation.
A few areas you may work on:
- Agent execution: Build harnesses, orchestration systems, and isolated environments where coding agents can safely execute long-running tasks.
- Tools and context: Give agents secure, observable access to codebases, tests, documentation, internal systems, and the tools needed to complete real engineering work.
- Agentic development workflows: Apply AI across planning, technical design, implementation, testing, code review, and production operations.
- Evaluation and validation: Build systems that test and review human- and agent-generated changes, catch regressions earlier, and improve confidence in autonomous development.
- Agent-native developer infrastructure: Design CI/CD, local development, APIs, CLIs, and platform tooling that can be operated directly by both engineers and agents.
- Internal builder platforms: Create reusable frameworks that let teams quickly build their own internal tools, dashboards, automations, and agents.

- Own the reliability, observability, security, performance, and cost of the systems you build.
- Help define how Decagon engineers-and increasingly autonomous agents-build and operate production software.

section_intro: About Decagon
section_about:
When a Fortune 500 hands its customer experience to an AI agent, it is one of the largest bets the business will make that year - and enterprises of that size do not make it on a demo.
Each customer has their own requirements for how an AI agent should be evaluated, and the narratives we build have to start there and hold up long after the decision is made.
Data plays a central role in almost every one of those narratives, which is why Agent Data Science exists.
A deployment is evaluated by many stakeholders inside the customer's organization, including senior leaders, customer experience teams, and technical functions, each with their own criteria for success.
You own how performance is defined, measured, and demonstrated against these criteria, from translating them into metrics we operationalize and deliver, to improving the ones that are key to each evaluation.
You hold that from the first pre-sales evaluation through the life of the account.
Our team sits within Agent Product Management and focuses mostly on our largest and most complex deployments, while supporting the data needs of Decagon customers more broadly.
We are small relative to that surface area, which means the scope you own is very wide and exceptionally cross-functional.
The work compounds accordingly: every metric you define on a flagship deployment becomes the default for the deals that follow, and the frameworks you build outlive any single account.
Demonstrating the value of our product is everyone's responsibility, not only ours.
So the primary leverage we create comes from making the rest of the organization better at it.
That is what lets us stay focused on the hardest and most novel measurement problems our customers bring us, which gives this team real influence over the long-term product roadmap.
Most of your time will be spent working directly with customers to establish what should be measured and then building what produces it.
Usually, the hard part comes from driving alignment, not the analysis itself.
You own both reporting on performance and improving it, working alongside the Agent Product Managers, Agent Strategy Managers, Strategic Account Directors, and Agent Deployment Engineers on each account.
Beyond the work you do with individual customers, you will build the product features and frameworks that make everyone else at Decagon better at this work.
This is a rare combination: the rigor of a strong quant, the presence of a trusted executive advisor, and the ownership of a founder.
If you have ever wanted to own the metric rather than report on it, this role was designed for you.
You are trusted to make high-stakes decisions independently and own outcomes.
section_responsibilities:
- Work directly with customers to define the metrics that will be used to measure performance, then operationalize them so that both sides use and trust them.
- Own the delivery of those metrics, where transparent access to data helps reinforce the narrative we build with the customer.
- Own improving the metrics that matter most on your accounts, from diagnosing what drives performance to designing the experiments and driving the changes that move them.
- Scope and build the product features, tools, and frameworks that empower the rest of Decagon to do more of this work themselves.
- Define what success looks like for new initiatives that have no precedent.
As Decagon's product continues to evolve, new surface areas will emerge where the right way to measure success has to be invented rather than applied.
- Run tight feedback loops into Product, Engineering, and Research, shaping the product based on what you learn measuring our most demanding deployments.
- 5+ years in data science, analytics, or another quantitative role where you drove analyses end to end and used them to move decisions, whether at a high-growth technology company, in consulting, or in a forward-deployed or solutions role.
- Exceptional judgment when interpreting metrics.
You think through the edge cases quickly, and you can see how the same number will be read by someone arguing for us and against us.
This includes 80/20 intuition on what's most important vs. analyzing everything.
- Comfort in fast-moving, ambiguous situations where you shape the approach as much as you implement it.
Given a question with no established right answer, you can identify the best available option and defend it.
- Strong independence.
You operate with very little day-to-day direction, set your own priorities against a broad mandate, and bring decisions rather than questions.
You are comfortable being the person who defines the work rather than the person who receives it.
- Ability to bring stakeholders to a shared definition of success, even when they arrive with different priorities and different levels of technical depth.
- Strong technical fundamentals.
Fluency in SQL and Python, and comfort working with large volumes of messy, unstructured conversational data.
Even better if you have
- A history of building internal tooling that gained meaningful adoption, and the judgment to recognize when a problem should stay a one-off.
- Experience working on AI products in production, including evaluating LLM or agent behavior and building the evaluations yourself.

section_intro: About Decagon
section_about:
Brand Design at Decagon shapes the visual identity of our company and helps define how we're perceived by customers, partners, and the broader AI community.
Our work turns sophisticated technology into clear, confident, and differentiated brand storytelling-across campaigns, content, web, and moments that shape perception.
We believe strong brands are built through taste, consistency, and conviction.
We care deeply about craft, narrative, cohesion, and expanding the brand into new, exciting territories while building its core.
Designers here grow by shipping work fast, operating with urgency, developing a strong point of view, and raising the bar together.
This role sits at the heart of Decagon's brand expression.
As a Brand Designer, you'll help shape how Decagon shows up in the world-how we tell our story, how we stand apart, and how our brand evolves as the company scales.
You'll work on marketing-led brand initiatives that influence perception and drive growth, contributing to both foundational brand work and high-visibility moments.
This role is ideal for a designer who is excited by storytelling, energized by momentum, and motivated by building a brand thoughtfully, not just executing individual assets.
You won't be handed a perfectly defined box.
Instead, you'll help define the edges-learning where to push, where to refine, and how to maintain coherence as the brand expands.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and art direct high-quality brand assets across campaigns, web, sales materials, video, events, social, and internal storytelling.
- Help evolve and expand Decagon's brand design system-bringing consistency while pushing into new, differentiated expressions.
- Contribute to brand strategy and messaging, and translate that thinking into clear and compelling visuals.
- Bring systems thinking and attention to detail to developing layouts, concepts, and executions.
- Iterate quickly based on feedback, often across multiple workstreams, balancing speed with polish.
- Bring references, inspiration, and creative ideas that help Decagon stand out.
- Maintain consistency and quality across all brand touchpoints.
- 4-6 years of experience in brand design, art direction, and marketing-focused creative roles.
- A portfolio that demonstrates strong visual taste, storytelling, and brand thinking.
- Proficient in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite, with a strong interest and curiosity in dabbling in AI design models and tools.
- Experience designing for marketing surfaces (web, campaigns, decks, events, content).
- Strong fundamentals in typography, layout, color, and hierarchy.
- Ability to interpret a brief and execute thoughtful, on-brand creative.
- Comfort working in high-velocity environments with evolving priorities.

- Some experience with filming and editing social content is a great-to-have.

- Proactive, business-minded, and committed to delivering practical solutions that support both compliance and commercial success.

- Law degree and qualification to practice law in Brazil.
- Native-level Portuguese and fluent English; Spanish is strongly preferred.
- 7+ years of relevant post-qualification legal experience (in-house experience in technology or SaaS strongly preferred).

HOW WE WORK
section_about:
Productions is the "done for you" managed services wing of ElevenLabs, built for creators and media businesses.
We bring together our AI audio tools and human experts in linguistics, mixing and post-production to deliver human-edited dubs, audiobooks and more in 15+ languages, directly on the ElevenLabs platform.
Our customers include global media broadcasters, publishers, gaming companies and major film studios.
We're hiring engineers to build the systems behind it: the platforms that let human expertise and AI work together at the quality our clients expect, and the labelling tools our research teams use to improve our models.
You'll own a scope in one of these areas:
- Human data platform: the labelling and evaluation platform research uses to continuously improve our models.
You'll ship new task editors, improve reliability, catch misuse and build the metrics behind higher-quality data pipelines.
- Core productions engine: the backend machine nobody sees but everybody relies on.
You'll build and maintain the services that run our production workflows, with room to lead projects.
- Editor platform: the professional editing tools our production teams work in.
You'll build in Rust, combining UI systems with a deep understanding of the underlying system.
We're building professional tools and core infrastructure, not consumer features.
The work is mostly building, with little hand-holding.
You'll carve out your own scope and own the outcome.
section_requirements:
- Strong backend engineering experience, ideally in functional programming languages like Rust, with a full-stack focus on designing UI systems.
You've shipped and run production systems end to end.
- Experience making systems reliable and scalable, such as internal platforms, workflow or task engines, or data pipelines.
You take pride in the infrastructure nobody sees but everybody relies on.
- Comfortable switching between building a new tool or editor and hardening the platform underneath it, and keen to lead projects when the opportunity arises.
- Opinionated and able to defend your ideas, but know when to just grind.
You're happy doing the unglamorous work, and you're hungry.
Bonus:
- Experience building editor or UI-heavy professional tools, with a systems-level understanding of what sits underneath.
- Experience with data labelling or annotation platforms, or managing crowdsourced workforces.
Location
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe and the US East Coast, with the ability to operate in GMT-5 to GMT+1 timezones required.
If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, Dublin, Amsterdam, and Warsaw.

- A cross-functional operator who can align paid media, design, engineering, and product teams around a shared optimization roadmap

- Experience optimizing PLG/self-serve funnels alongside sales-assisted (demo/contact-sales) funnels

We are seeking an experienced Privacy Program Manager to join our Legal Team and help build and scale ElevenLabs' global privacy program.
In this role, you will translate privacy requirements into effective, repeatable processes across the company and drive the day-to-day operation of key privacy initiatives.
You will work closely with Legal, Product, Engineering, Security, Safety, and GTM teams to operationalize privacy-by-design, manage privacy assessments and compliance workflows, and strengthen the systems and processes that support ElevenLabs' growing global business.
This role is ideal for someone who combines deep privacy program experience with strong project management skills and enjoys building scalable programs in a fast-moving AI environment.
section_responsibilities:
- Manage and continuously improve ElevenLabs' global privacy program, translating legal and regulatory requirements into scalable operational processes and controls.
- Own and coordinate privacy compliance workflows across frameworks including GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, US state privacy laws, HIPAA, and applicable biometric privacy requirements.
- Manage privacy impact assessment processes, including Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), and assessments involving AI systems, biometric data, voice technologies, health information, and other sensitive data.
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Legal, and Security teams to operationalize privacy-by-design throughout the product development lifecycle.
- Maintain data inventories, records of processing activities (RoPAs), data flow documentation, and other privacy governance records.
- Manage processes for data subject and consumer rights requests, including access, deletion, correction, and opt-out requests, and help ensure requests are handled consistently and within applicable deadlines.
- Partner with Security and Legal on third-party and vendor privacy assessments, data processing requirements, and privacy-related risk remediation.
- Support privacy incident response and regulatory or customer inquiries by coordinating documentation, stakeholders, timelines, and follow-up actions.
- Implement and administer privacy tooling and automation to improve the efficiency and scalability of privacy operations including maintaining ElevenLabs' consent management platform and partnering with Legal, Marketing, Product, and Engineering to ensure cookie, tracking technology, and other consent and preference mechanisms are appropriately configured, documented, monitored, and updated as our products and regulatory requirements evolve.
- Develop privacy program metrics, dashboards, and reporting to track compliance, identify risks, and communicate program maturity and priorities to stakeholders.
- Develop and maintain privacy policies, procedures, playbooks, templates, and internal guidance.
- Coordinate privacy training and awareness initiatives across the company.
section_requirements:
- Excited by AI and emerging technologies and interested in solving novel privacy challenges involving voice, biometrics, health information, and other sensitive data.
- An exceptional program manager who can turn complex requirements into clear workstreams, owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
- Comfortable operating across Legal, Product, Engineering, Security, and commercial teams and able to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Highly organized and detail-oriented, while able to prioritize effectively and maintain momentum across multiple workstreams.
- Pragmatic and solutions-oriented, with a strong instinct for building processes that manage risk without creating unnecessary friction.
- Comfortable building programs and processes from the ground up in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
WHAT YOU BRING
- 6+ years of experience in privacy program management, privacy operations, data governance, compliance, or a related field, ideally within a technology, SaaS, or AI company.
- Demonstrated experience operationalizing privacy requirements under frameworks such as GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other US state privacy laws as well as sector specific frameworks such as HIPAA and biometric privacy requirements.
- Technical mindset, you can read a data flow diagram, understand system architectures and keys to data handling and can translate between legal requirements and engineering implementation.
- Experience building or significantly improving privacy review processes, privacy impact assessments, or privacy control frameworks.
- Hands-on experience managing consent management platforms and cookie/tracking technology compliance, including consent configuration, preference management, and coordination with technical and marketing teams.
- Familiarity with security and privacy frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar.
- Privacy certifications such as CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CIPM, or CIPT are a plus.
- Excellent project management, communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.
LOCATION
This role is remote and can be executed in the United States.
We have a strong preference for the Eastern time zone, ideally New York.

You will own the transformation layer between raw data and business decisions: modelling our data in dbt, defining the certified metrics the company runs on, and setting the standards that every analyst and data scientist at ElevenLabs builds.

- Experience serving data to LLM-based agents or building semantic / metrics layers consumed by AI tools.
- Experience with CI for data (Slim CI, data contracts, PII policy tags) and infrastructure-as-code for warehouse access.
LOCATION
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe, with the ability to operate in GMT and GMT+1 timezones.

section_intro:
As the Product Compliance Engineer at Figure AI, you will play a pivotal role in developing the safety certification and compliance strategy for the Figure product line.
You will drive end-to-end safety and regulatory compliance from early system design through certification and commercial launch.
You will work cross‐functionally with mechanical, electrical, controls, software, manufacturing, and legal teams to ensure the robot is safe, certifiable, and ready for deployment in real‐world human environments.
section_responsibilities:
Own the end-to-end product safety certification and compliance strategy for shipping the humanoid robot and ecosystem products into the real world.
Navigate the various mandatory and analogous safety standards (UL, IEC, ISO, CE, FCC, etc.) and define the right certification roadmap for Figure.
Drive testing and certification efforts across all aspects of the product line serving as the primary interface to NRTLs, test labs, and certification bodies.
Apply industry-standard safety methodologies to ensure the integration of safety and certification considerations throughout the product development lifecycle, from design to deployment.
Lead hazard analysis activities such as HARA, FMEA and FTA.
Translate hazards into verifiable safety requirements across hardware, software, and controls.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to validate safety requirements in both development and mass production settings.

Strong working knowledge of product safety and functional safety standards.
Hands‐on experience leading UL / IEC / CE certification programs from design through approval.
Ability to work collaboratively across mechanical, electrical and software domains.
Bonus
Proven ability to perform and lead hazard and risk analyses and convert results into engineering requirements
Advanced Degree in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.

Design and validate PCBAs for charging products, including both the power stages and the mixed-signal control boards.

Experience with Altium.

section_intro:
Our Manufacturing team is looking for a Production Lead to help drive daily execution on the factory floor.
In this role, you'll work closely with supervisors, engineers, and quality teams to deliver against production schedules while ensuring the highest standards of safety, quality, and efficiency.
You'll be hands-on, coordinating work across teams, resolving issues in real time, and stepping onto the line when needed to keep builds on track.
Shift Schedule: 2pm-10:30pm
section_responsibilities:
Lead by example to maintain a safe, clean, and compliant work environment.
Assign daily tasks and coordinate resources to meet production schedules and quality targets.
Monitor production flow, track progress, and provide updates on priority work orders.
Verify readiness of lines, components, and equipment; support set-ups and changeovers.
Assist with troubleshooting and resolving quality, equipment, or process issues.
Review and complete production documentation to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Conduct shift passdowns and cross-functional updates.
Support employee training and development; step in for absent operators when needed.
Partner with supervisors to drive Lean Manufacturing initiatives and continuous improvement.
section_requirements:
AS degree or equivalent experience (high school diploma or GED required).
3+ years in a regulated manufacturing environment, with 1+ year in a leadership role.
Hands-on experience in assembly, manufacturing, or production (robotics, automotive, aerospace, or electronics preferred).
Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with attention to detail.
Ability to collaborate across teams and deliver against production goals.
Excellent communication and time management skills.
Comfortable lifting up to 50 lbs., working with hand tools, and handling chemicals with PPE.
The US base salary range for this full-time position is $80,000 to $105,000 per year.
The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

job_title: Global Supply Manager, EE and Semiconductors
section_intro:
As a Global Supply Manager (GSM) for EE & Semiconductors, you are a technical and commercial leader responsible for the foundational supply chain of our humanoid robot.
You will develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy for essential components and materials, managing the lifecycle from pre-concept through to the handoff to sustaining operations.
Your mission is to align business needs with supplier capabilities while navigating the complex, high-stakes landscape of semiconductor technologies.
section_responsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing & Roadmap Execution
Global Strategy: Develop and execute a comprehensive sourcing strategy for essential components and materials, ensuring long-term scalability for our humanoid robot.
Roadmap Alignment: Create and manage a semiconductor technology roadmap that aligns our product architecture with future industry trends and supplier innovations.
AVL Ownership: Own the Approved Vendor List (AVL) and lead the full supplier lifecycle-from identification and qualification to performance evaluation.
Humanoid Robotics Ecosystem & Supply Agreements
Long-Term Agreements: Negotiate high-stakes, long-term deals and strategic supply agreements that secure the high-priority materials required to build and scale our humanoid platform.
Cross-Functional Synergy: Collaborate closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, and NPI teams to ensure sourcing activities remain perfectly synchronized with product development and production timelines.
Market Intelligence: Stay ahead of industry trends, pricing dynamics, lead-time fluctuations, and technical advancements within the global silicon and electronics markets.
Technical Influence & BOM Optimization
BOM Scrubs: Lead rigorous BOM scrubs and analysis to identify end-of-life (EOL) risks, single-source vulnerabilities, and technical bottlenecks before design freeze.
Design Influence: Partner with Architecture and Engineering to influence design decisions for optimal cost, performance, and supply-chain resilience.
Should-Cost Modeling: Own the "Should-Cost" modeling process to drive aggressive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) reductions through negotiation and value engineering.
Risk Management & Commercial Leadership
Risk Mitigation: Identify vulnerabilities in the EE supply chain (e.g., geopolitical shifts, capacity constraints) and implement robust hedging and business continuity strategies.
Contract Negotiation: Negotiate Master Purchase Agreements (MPAs), quality agreements, and Statements of Work (SOWs) that secure competitive pricing and favorable terms.
Performance Metrics: Implement and maintain robust supplier performance metrics and lead periodic business reviews to ensure strategic objectives are met.
Supplier Development: Periodically travel to supplier sites to drive initiatives such as cost reductions, relationship building, and supplier development.
section_requirements:
Experience: 7+ years in global sourcing or commodity management, specifically with semiconductor or complex EE components.
Education: BS in Engineering (EE preferred), Supply Chain, or Business Management.
Category Expertise (Required): Direct experience managing and sourcing in at least one or two of the following segments:
Computing: Processors (CPUs/GPUs/FPGAs) and Memory (DRAM/NAND).
Perception: Sensors (IMUs, Lidar, Vision Sensors) and Camera Modules.
Power & Motion: Power Management ICs (PMICs), Battery Management Systems (BMS), and Motor Controllers.
Connectivity: Interface ICs (USB, PCIe, Ethernet), Wireless (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/5G), and high-speed Signal Integrity components.
Interaction: Display technologies, touch interfaces.
Domain Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of the semiconductor ecosystem and experience in NPI (New Product Introduction) environments.
Negotiation: Proven track record of securing long-term agreements with Tier 1 global suppliers.
Autonomy: Ability to operate as a subject-matter expert with a high degree of autonomy, balancing technical problem-solving with strategic planning.
Relationship Management: Skilled at establishing strong relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
Travel : Ability to travel domestically and internationally 25%
The US base salary range for this full-time position is $140,000 to $220,000 per year.
The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

section_intro:
We are looking for a Wire Harness Technician.
In this role, you will be highly focused on designing and building wire harnesses and custom cables to enable test setups required for rapid iteration across development, validation, and integration efforts.
You will operate in a fast-paced prototyping and low-volume environment, building production-quality harnesses as well as on-demand, non-standard cable solutions that directly unblock engineering and testing teams.
You will build harnesses from drawings, BOMs, and work orders while meeting IPC/WHMA standards and aggressive delivery timelines.
section_responsibilities:
Build build-to-print and custom wire harnesses, including cut, strip, crimp, solder, braid/sleeve, heat-shrink, basic potting, and final terminations.
Create custom cables and harnesses on demand to support test setups, debugging, EVT/DVT activities, and rapid hardware iteration, often with evolving or incomplete requirements.
Partner closely with engineering and test teams to quickly translate test needs into practical cable and harness solutions.
Read and follow drawings, schematics, BOMs, work orders, and ECOs; record traceability in ERP/routers.
Crimp and verify terminals/contacts (TE/AMP, Molex, JST, Amphenol/LEMO, etc.) with specified tooling; document pull tests when required.
Print and apply labels and heat-shrink markers per print.
Perform electrical tests: continuity, insulation/hipot, and basic troubleshooting with DMMs, cable testers, and fixtures.
Execute rework to spec (e.g., IPC/WHMA-A-620) and support NCMR/MRB containment.
Maintain 5S/ESD and safety standards; proactively suggest process, tooling, and DFM improvements-especially for testability and iteration speed.
section_requirements:
2-5+ years building wire harnesses and cable assemblies in manufacturing or prototyping environments.
Strong ability to independently design and execute custom cable builds for test and prototype use.
Ability to read prints/schematics and follow work instructions with minimal supervision.
Proficiency in crimping and soldering (selective tinning, shields/drain wires, coax, twisted pair).
Hands-on experience with tooling: strippers, gauges, pull testers, manual/pneumatic crimpers (Daniels or similar), soldering stations, heat guns.
Working knowledge of IPC/WHMA-A-620 (Class 2/3) and familiarity with J-STD-001.
Strong quality and schedule focus, with high first-pass yield and low rework in fast-iteration environments.
Bonus
Current IPC/WHMA-A-620 or J-STD-001 certifications.
Experience supporting test labs, EVT/DVT builds, and rapid iteration cycles.
Experience with cable testers (e.g., Cirris) and basic fixture integration.
Exposure to ECOs/NPI, startup environments, and creating or maintaining SOPs.
Basic comfort with CAD viewers for drawing review and ERP systems for traceability.
Bilingual English/Spanish.
The US base pay range for this full-time position is $30.00 to $50.00 per hour.
The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

job_title: Design Verification Engineer, TPU, Silicon, Google Cloud
section_intro:
In this role, you'll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration.
You will have an opportunity to drive TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) technology that powers Google's most demanding AI/ML applications.
You'll be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's TPU.
You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide, and leverage your design and verification expertise to verify complex digital designs, with a specific focus on TPU architecture and its integration within AI/ML-driven systems.
In this role, you will own the full verification life-cycle from verification planning and test execution to coverage closure, with an emphasis on meeting stringent AI/ML performance and accuracy goals, build constrained-random verification environments capable of exposing corner-case bugs and ensuring the reliability of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) workloads on Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) hardware.
You will collaborate closely with design and verification engineers in active projects and perform verification.
We're the driving team behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future.
section_responsibilities:
Plan the verification of digital design blocks and interact with design engineers to identify important verification scenarios.
Identify and write all types of coverage measures for stimulus and corner-cases.
Debug tests with design engineers to deliver functionally correct design blocks.
Measure to identify verification holes and to show progress towards tape-out.
Create a constrained-random verification environment using SystemVerilog and Universal Verification Methodology (UVM).
section_requirements:

4 years of experience in verification, verifying digital logic at RTL level using SystemVerilog or Specman/E for Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) or ASICs.
Experience verifying digital systems using standard IP components/interconnects (e.g., microprocessor cores, hierarchical memory subsystems).
Experience in verification and debug of IP/subsystem/SoCs in the networking domain such as packet processing, bandwidth management, congestion control.
section_preferred:
Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
Experience with industry-standard simulators, revision control systems, and regression systems.
Experience in Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) accelerators or vector processing units.
Experience with the full verification life cycle.
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills.

job_title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Advanced Technology and Innovation
location: Sunnyvale, CA, USA; Austin, TX, USA; Kirkland, WA, USA; New York, NY, USA; Reston, VA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Seattle, WA, USA
section_intro:
Our thirst for technology is a part of everything we do.
The Data Center Engineering team takes the physical design of our data centers into the future.
Our lab mirrors a research and development department -- cutting-edge strategies are born, tested and tested again.
Along with a team of great minds, you take on complex topics like how we use power or how to run state-of-the-art, environmentally-friendly facilities.
You're a visionary who optimizes for efficiencies and never stops seeking improvements -- even small changes that can make a huge impact.
You generate ideas, communicate recommendations to senior-level executives and drive implementation alongside facilities technicians.
With your technical expertise, you ensure compliance with codes and standards, develop infrastructure improvements and serve as an expert in your specialty (e.g., cooling, electrical).
As part of the global controls team, you will work with experts and innovators in the data center industry.
You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project managing, and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS).
Using Google leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space.
Google Data centers have multiple components such as generators, UPS, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, etc.
All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open or proprietary communications protocols.
The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center.
The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.
US: $121000 - $174000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
section_responsibilities:
Perform root cause analysis and corrective actions for Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) to maintain data center operations.
Lead the full life cycle of controls projects, including developing scopes of work, budgets, and schedules, and managing the execution of system improvements.
Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces while iterating on Sequences of Operation (SOO) with design teams.
Provide technical guidance, training, and assistance to internal customers while supporting procurement activities and vendor proposal reviews.
Conduct regular site visits to supervise vendor performance and ensure compliance with design specifications, safety protocols, and local codes.
section_requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
3 years of experience working on critical infrastructure projects related to process improvements.
Experience with mission critical systems and operations (e.g., power generation, data center, refinery, chip fabrication, chemical plant processing, etc.).
Experience implementing controls engineering.
section_preferred:
Master's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or other related engineering field.
Experience designing, configuring, programming, installing and troubleshooting BMS and Electrical Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems application specific controllers and software such as Ignition and Factory Talk.
Experience with TCP/IP, EtherNet IP, BacNet or MODBUS, IEC 61850 communication protocol.
Experience with management of change, productivity suite and project management software.
Understanding of engineering documentation, Property Management System (PMS)/BMS drawings and standard operating procedures.
Excellent communication, teamwork, organizational and problem-solving skills with a track record for cultivating strong relationships with internal stakeholders, vendors, or customers.

job_title: Senior Silicon Engineer, HBM Memory Subsystem Design, Integration and Validation
section_intro:
In this role, you'll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration.
You will have an opportunity to drive cutting-edge TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) technology that powers Google's most demanding AI/ML applications.
You'll be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's TPU.
You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide, and leverage your design and verification expertise to verify complex digital designs, with a specific focus on TPU architecture and its integration within AI/ML-driven systems.
In this role, you will be part of a team developing ASICs used to accelerate and improve traffic efficiency in data centers.
You will collaborate with members of architecture, verification, power and performance, and physical design to deliver high quality designs for next generation data center accelerators.
You will solve technical problems with innovative micro-architecture and practical logic solutions, and evaluate design options with complexity, performance, power and area in mind.
We're the driving team behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future.
section_responsibilities:
Define microarchitecture and develop high-quality RTL for memory controller frontends, guiding implementation trade-offs across performance, area, power, timing, and configurability for multi-channel and pseudo-channel configurations.
Lead the design, integration, and delivery of complex memory controller backends and HBM/DDR PHY macros, owning quality closure (DFI pipe wrappers, clock/reset, PLL references, sideband bridging) and schedule from concept to tapeout.
Collaborate with DV teams to build test plans, improve coverage, and validate design intent (UVM, emulation, ECC/RAS error injection), while tracking JEDEC specs and memory conferences for the latest HBM trends.
Lead and support ATE testing, first-silicon lab bring-up, and physical characterization of the HBM PHY and controller across PVT (process, voltage, temperature) corners.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to engineers while promoting best practices in RTL design, review, documentation, methodology, and systematic root-cause debug.
section_requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10 years of experience in memory subsystem design, integration or verification.
Experience with DRAM protocols (HBM2e/HBM3/HBM4 or DDR/LPDDR4x/5/5X) including Joint Electron Device Engineering Council (JEDEC) timing, refresh and training sequences.
Experience with the DFI controller-to-PHY interface, leading a feature or IP block, and mentoring engineers.
Experience in SystemVerilog RTL, simulation and debug flows.
section_preferred:
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience delivering configurable, reusable IP-parameterization, release packaging, integration guides and customer-facing documentation.
Experience integrating third-party controller and PHY IP (Rambus, Cadence/Synopsys class) into production silicon.
Experience with SECDED per pseudo-channel, Reed-Solomon symbol correction, error queues, lane/row repair, address-folded CRC.
Experience with UVM methodology and emulation-based pre-silicon validation, and familiarity with memory telemetry and Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) - per-pseudo-channel counters, link availability, continuous eye-opening monitors.

job_title: Research Scientist, Modeling of Readout and Reset, Quantum
location: Goleta, CA, USA; Los Angeles, CA, USA
section_intro:
As an organization, Google maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals, while providing individuals and teams the freedom to emphasize specific types of work.
As a Research Scientist, you'll setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly, managing deadlines and deliverables while applying the latest theories to develop new and improved products, processes, or technologies.
From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, our research scientists work on real-world problems that span the breadth of computer science, such as machine (and deep) learning, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more.
As a Research Scientist, you'll also actively contribute to the wider research community by sharing and publishing your findings, with ideas inspired by internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world.
Google Quantum AI's goal is to build a practically useful quantum computer.
Modeling of readout and reset team aims at quantitative understanding of error mechanisms of these operations, resulting in operation improvement and development of new schemes with advanced performance.
Google Quantum AI is building quantum computing for otherwise unsolvable problems.
The full potential of quantum computing will be unlocked with a large-scale computer capable of complex, error-corrected computations.
Our roadmap is focused on advancing the capabilities of quantum computing and enabling meaningful applications.
section_responsibilities:
Develop models for readout and reset in superconducting qubits, including numerical models of physical processes causing errors.
Validate models with experimental results for system optimization and design.
Collaborate closely with the hardware team to analyze and theoretically understand experimental data.
Develop and maintain software and integrate it with data-taking infrastructure.
Propose and analyze prospective readout and reset schemes with advanced performance.
section_requirements:
PhD degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience with modeling of qubit systems.
Experience in programming using Python.
One of more scientific publication submission(s) for conferences, journals, or public repositories related to Quantum computing.
section_preferred:
Experience with modeling superconducting qubit operations, particularly readout and reset.
Experience with numerical simulations of quantum systems and with high-performance computing tools.
Experience collaborating with experimentalists on quantum computing projects or analyzing/modeling experimental data.
Experience with microwave engineering of superconducting qubits.
Experience with error correction codes.
Familiarity with circuit Quantum Electrodynamics (cQED).

Zero-touch provisioning through Apple Business Manager and Autopilot, automated onboarding and offboarding, hardware refreshes, DLP, and forensics.
Where the lifecycle still depends on someone remembering to do something, replace that with code.
- Build the automation the fleet runs on.
Most of this role's leverage comes from tooling - Python and scripts against Jamf, Intune, and Okta APIs, event-driven workflows, and self-service that lets employees fix their own problems.
- Partner with Security on endpoint posture.

- Be the final escalation for endpoint issues.
IT Operations handles tier 1 and 2 globally; the problems that reach you are the strange ones.
You'll fix them, and then fix the class of problem so the next person doesn't file the ticket.
- Support a global, in-person-heavy company.

- Strong scripting and automation ability in Python, Bash, or Swift, with a track record of building tooling against vendor APIs rather than clicking through admin consoles.

- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth, and global environment.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
The Business Development team leads Harvey's partnerships with the cloud hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, inference providers, data suppliers, and emerging open source ecosystem.
These are multi-dimensional relationships: the same companies we build with are also the ones we build on and go to market alongside.
Our work spans commercial deal structuring, co-selling, co-development, and co-marketing, working cross-functionally with Finance, Research, Product, Sales, Marketing, and other teams across the company.
As a member of the Cloud & AI team, you will help drive strategic partner initiatives and engagement ranging from new model releases and product launch announcements to commercial agreements and co-marketing campaigns, and own the tactical execution that follows: activating commercial marketplaces, unlocking channel GTM opportunities, accelerating field enablement, and supporting day-to-day requests.
It is a unique opportunity that gives you a front row seat to how fast-growing AI companies work together to drive mutual growth.
This is a zero to one builder role on a team that will grow alongside the partner portfolio.
You will be tasked with working across a wide range of programs and initiatives, including standing up new operational processes and ongoing partner reporting.
Much of what this role touches does not have a defined playbook yet.
The ideal candidate is a strong operator who can bring structure to complex partnerships, move comfortably between strategic work and hands-on execution, and build programs that scale as the team grows.
section_responsibilities:
PARTNER RELATIONSHIP & COMMERCIAL MANAGEMENT
- Serve as a go-to resource for multiple cloud, frontier lab, and inference & data partners, and act as a consistent point of contact across internal and external teams
- Run regular partner business reviews and joint planning sessions, including quarterly goal setting and executive involvement
- Support commercial negotiations, including business case development and deal structuring, working closely with Finance, Product, and Research through to signature
- Track partner activity, program performance, and progress against joint plans, and provide clear updates to stakeholders
JOINT GO-TO-MARKET & CO-SELLING
- Run the co-sell motion with select partners: drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue by designing plays that build momentum with field teams (account mapping, deal registration, pipeline reviews, and alignment with Harvey's sales org)
- Activate and operate Harvey's presence on commercial cloud marketplaces, including listings, private offers, and the operational workflows behind them
- Support Harvey's sales team on individual partner-supported opportunities by bringing in the right partner contacts, unlocking partner resources, and clearing blockers
- Build enablement materials for both sides: partner-facing Harvey narratives, and internal guides on how to sell with each partner
CO-DEVELOPMENT & CO-MARKETING
- Coordinate joint technical programs with partners, connecting Harvey's Research and Product teams with their counterparts and keeping feedback moving in both directions
- Support product launch co-announcements, lining up timing, messaging, and approvals across Harvey Marketing and partner communications teams
- Launch joint marketing programs with partners: case studies, webinars, events, and co-branded content
- Maximize Harvey's standing in partner programs to unlock funding, technical resources, and go-to-market support
BUILDING THE FUNCTION
- Contribute to the operational foundation of the team, including portfolio tracking, partner plans, pipeline reporting, and regular reporting cadences with leadership
- Develop repeatable processes and internal frameworks for how partnerships are evaluated, launched, and reviewed, so that programs stay scalable as the team grows
- Keep internal teams across Sales, Product, Research, Marketing, and Finance current on partner activity through regular updates and business reviews
- Take on new scope as the partner portfolio and the team expand over time
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years of professional experience in partnerships, alliances, sales, business development or corporate development, ideally at a high-growth company where programs were in their infancy and the partner motion was still being built
- Experience structuring or managing complex alliances or partnerships, including commercial negotiations
- Experience or knowledge of commercial marketplaces, including listings, private offers, and deal transaction mechanics
- Track record of sourcing or influencing revenue through partner channels, ideally with ownership of a pipeline or revenue target
- Experience across co-selling, co-marketing, and co-development, with a feel for the nuanced dynamics of partners who are suppliers, channels, and product enablers
- Understanding of the AI ecosystem: the major cloud providers and frontier labs, how models are served and priced, and the emerging players across each market
- Strong program management skills, including the ability to manage multiple workstreams, establish clear owners and timelines, and lead initial ideation through execution
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to synthesize complex information and communicate clear recommendations to executives
- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward building when there's no existing process to follow, and the ability to influence without authority across teams

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
As Workplace Specialist, you are Harvey's Workplace team in Toronto.
You run the office end to end: the space, the service partners behind it, the experience employees and clients have in it, and the front door.
You are the person everyone in the office turns to, and the one who actually knows.
Your manager sits in another office and time zone.
You take priorities and standards from them and from the global Workplace team, then run the office with real independence.
You escalate the calls that need a manager: contract terms, spend above your authority, and anything with cost, risk, or precedent attached.
Our Toronto office is a serviced suite at iQ Offices, 302 Bay Street.
Much of your building work runs through the iQ team rather than a traditional landlord, and as Toronto grows you will help shape what the next space needs.
This is a fully in-office role, Monday through Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm, with flexibility for early setups, events, and the occasional after-hours matter.
section_responsibilities:
The Office Standard
- Hold the office to the standard the Workplace team sets for appearance, cleanliness, and readiness, and flag what is slipping before it becomes visible
- Walk the office daily and find maintenance needs, safety concerns, and service gaps before anyone reports them
- Be the first person anyone asks about how the space works
Building & Facilities
- Hold the day-to-day relationship with iQ Offices and building management: work orders, approvals, access, and follow-through
- Manage facilities issues (HVAC, plumbing, lighting, doors, appliances, repairs), managing iQ through resolution, and confirm the fix held
- Coordinate deliveries, freight, and loading dock bookings within the building's rules
- Escalate any building matter that carries cost, risk, or precedent to your manager
Vendors & Food and Beverage
- Keep the Toronto vendor book current: contacts, scopes, performance notes, COIs, and renewal dates
- Hold vendors to scope, address service issues directly, and escalate patterns rather than incidents
- Run the pantry, snack, coffee, and catered lunch program; track consumption and cost per head
- Source local Toronto vendors for catering, supplies, and services as the office grows
Front of House & Guests
- Own the front door: greet employees, candidates, and clients, and manage the visitor experience end to end
- Issue and revoke employee badges and keep building access accurate, to the policy set by Workplace and Security
- Receive and route mail, packages, and couriers
- Arrange cover through iQ reception or a backup plan agreed with your manager when you are out
Employee Experience & Events
- Plan and run Toronto onsite events, celebrations, team lunches, and all-hands viewing logistics, end to end
- Deliver client and executive visits: room sets, catering, AV readiness, and the details that make Harvey look sharp
- Host travelling employees and leaders from other offices, so desks, access, and logistics are ready before they land
Onboarding
- Run the Toronto new hire Day 1: desk setup, badges, building access, welcome, office tour, and swag
- Partner with People Ops and IT so every new hire is set up before they arrive
Space, Supplies & Budget
- Keep the seating chart accurate and execute moves, adds, and changes
- Track desk utilization and flag capacity pressure early, with the data behind it
- Own office supply inventory and ordering, including first aid and emergency supplies
- Submit new and recurring POs via our Procurement platform
- Track Toronto Workplace spend against budget (invoices, POs, cost per head), and partner with Finance on payment
Safety & Compliance
- Execute the emergency preparedness program: maintain the floor warden roster, join building drills, and coordinate with building life safety
- Serve as first responder during a workplace incident and report it through the process your manager owns
- Keep the office aligned with Ontario workplace health and safety requirements (for example, required postings and first aid kits), with support from People Ops
Systems & the Global Team
- Administer Workplace tools day to day (ticketing, seating, visitor management) and keep records accurate
- Own the Toronto Workplace request queue: resolve what you can, route what belongs to IT, People Ops, or Security
- Document how Toronto runs in SOPs and the site playbook, so anyone could pick it up cold
- Adopt global Workplace programs and standards locally, and tell the team where Toronto needs something different
- Partner with IT on conference room and AV readiness
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 4+ years in workplace operations, office management, facilities, or hospitality, including time as the primary or only Workplace person on site
- Breadth across facilities, vendors, front of house, events, and onboarding.
You are as comfortable with a work order as with a client visit
- Direct experience managing vendors and holding them to scope, including the difficult conversation when service slips
- A foundational understanding of office systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lighting), enough to describe a problem accurately and judge whether the fix held
- Experience with event and hospitality execution: catering, setups, and the details guests notice
- Comfort tracking spend, invoices, and POs, and turning day-to-day data into a clear picture for your manager
- Strong judgment working with a remote manager: you know what to handle, what to flag, and how to keep them informed without being chased
- Clear, professional written and verbal communication
- A self-starter who builds process where none exists yet
- Calm and resourceful when things go sideways, with no one down the hall to hand it to
- Genuine care for how the space feels to the people in it
- Knowledge of the Toronto vendor market and Ontario workplace requirements is a strong plus
- Experience in a serviced or flex office environment, or supporting an office opening or expansion, is a strong plus

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to help define and scale how Harvey brings its products to market.
At Harvey, Senior PMMs operate as owners of their product area or customer segment.
You will define positioning and narrative, shape go-to-market strategy, influence product direction and prioritization through deep customer, market, and competitive insight, and be accountable for driving adoption and revenue impact.
You should be equally comfortable shaping high-level positioning and go-to-market strategy as you are rolling up your sleeves to turn that strategy into content, launches, and enablement that drive real adoption.
This is a high-visibility role that works closely with Marketing, GTM, Product, and executive leadership to drive meaningful customer and business outcomes.
section_responsibilities:
- Lead go-to-market strategy for a core product area from positioning and narrative through launch and post-launch adoption
- Define clear, differentiated positioning and messaging grounded in customer needs, market dynamics, and product capabilities
- Plan and execute product and feature launches in close partnership with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Enablement
- Ensure launches translate into real-world impact through enablement, campaigns, and post-launch iteration
- Partner with Growth, Demand Gen, and Sales to support sustained adoption beyond initial launch moments
- Create and oversee high-impact customer- and sales-facing assets (e.g., pitch decks, one-pagers, competitive narratives, battlecards, onboarding materials)
- Conduct and synthesize customer research, market analysis, and competitive intelligence to inform positioning, GTM strategy, and product direction
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 6-8+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Product Management, Product Strategy, ideally in high growth B2B SaaS
- Experience marketing to enterprise customers, ideally including Fortune 100 or professional services organizations
- Proven track record leading major product launches and shaping positioning that drives real business outcomes
- Strong ability to translate technical or AI-powered products into clear, compelling narratives for diverse audiences
- Eager to move fast & drive impact, you'd rather build an imperfect one-pager quickly that is used by many people than a perfect one that collects dust
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong executive presence
- Ability to differentiate valuable signal from noise
- Ability to thrive in ambiguous cross-functional projects across Product, GTM, and Founders

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We're looking for a Lead Product Owner, Finance Systems to own the systems and workflows that power Harvey's finance organization as we scale globally.
This role sits at the center of our finance technology portfolio: NetSuite as the ERP core, Zip for procurement intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex for spend and card programs, and Metronome for usage-based billing.
You'll help shape the roadmap across that portfolio, prioritize competing demands, and drive changes from discovery through deployment, all in an agile and high-growth environment.
You'll partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Procurement, and Tax, as well as teams across Business Technology (where the Finance Systems team lives) and Security, to translate business needs into scalable, well-governed solutions.
This role is as much advisory as it is technical and hands-on: you'll bring thought leadership to the finance org, sit with stakeholders to understand complex and often ambiguous business problems, solution design the tools and automations, and then execute hands-on in the toolstack.
section_responsibilities:
- Act as the product owner for one or more of Harvey's core finance business process areas (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), along with the systems that serve them.
Run discovery with process owners, define target-state process and system design, own the roadmap, and measure success based on value add output and accuracy.
- Lead the hardest problems in your domain, where there's no established pattern to configure against.
That could be international expansion and the entity, currency, tax, and statutory complexity that comes with it, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Develop and maintain a holistic architecture strategy for the finance applications ecosystem: where each system's boundaries sit, how data moves between them, and what Harvey will need short, mid and long term.
Work with the owners of adjacent enterprise systems, including Workday and Salesforce, on the integrations and handoffs finance depends on.
- Find manual work and eliminate it, replacing spreadsheets, manual data entry, and email-based approvals with core configuration, automated workflows and integrations.
Evaluate new functionality within existing and/or new tooling for best fit at Harvey.
- Configure, maintain, and optimize NetSuite and, dependent on business process ownership determined, own the spend and revenue system workflows that feed the ledger: Zip intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex card programs and expenses, Metronome usage ingestion and downstream invoicing logic, and future tooling for advanced revenue recognition.
Understand, advise and execute on data flows, as well as the upstream product and company-wide data sources that revenue reporting depends on.
- Identify, test, and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across the processes you own in a controlled manner, with clear resulting impact of time savings and manual output eliminated.
- Own quality across your applications, ensuring lightweight SDLC to balance accuracy and agility.
Partner with leadership to set best practices and serve as the mentor and escalation point for peers across Finance and Business Technology on the portfolio's hardest design questions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 7+ years of hands-on experience as a finance systems professional, including 5+ years of direct NetSuite experience with demonstrated complex configuration depth and supporting a global, multi-entity and multi-currency finance organization.
- Product owner or product manager experience in at least one core finance business process area (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), with extensive depth in that domain: discovery with process owners, target-state process design, proposing tradeoffs or workarounds, and owning a roadmap through delivery.
Familiarity with the adjacent areas matters more than equal depth in all three.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at various levels of the business and technology organizations: adapting how you make a case depending on the audience, building alignment across cross-functional teams, and saying no to a request and explaining why.
A track record of mentoring peers, setting technical standards, or being the expert others escalate to on hard problems.
- Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, high-stakes process problems without an existing playbook, operating with a high degree of autonomy while knowing when to pull others in on high-impact decisions.
Examples include international expansion and multi-entity or multi-currency complexity, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Deep understanding of leading and emerging trends in SaaS finance applications and architecture, including where automation and AI are truly driving innovation.
- Direct experience implementing best practices around change management, regression and UAT planning, segregation of duties, and regulatory requirements, while increasing efficiencies.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey's Legal Engineers are skilled lawyers from top-tier law firms who apply their legal experience to ensure that current and prospective customers understand how Harvey's solutions enhance specific day-to-day workflows, working alongside Harvey's Account Executives to support all aspects of our sales strategy.
Legal Engineers build consultative relationships with law firm partners and associates and in-house attorneys at private equity firms and Fortune 500 companies, becoming trusted advisors on how Harvey's AI solutions can make them more effective.
Similar to how Solutions Architects secure the "technical win" in the sales process, Legal Engineers secure the "legal win" by performing in-depth customer discovery and education on Harvey's solutions through targeted meetings and demos that resonate with the customer's day-to-day workflows specific to their legal practice area.
Legal Engineers utilize their experience practicing law and their legal mindset to ask thoughtful questions to understand the needs of law firm and in-house attorneys, develop credibility, and then partner with Account Executives to educate them on Harvey's value via large and small group sessions as well as one-to-one conversations.
section_responsibilities:
- Engage with English- and German-speaking lawyers at existing and prospective customers to understand their workflow challenges, strategic objectives, and broader firm context - then demonstrate how Harvey's AI solutions can address them.
- Establish yourself as a credible expert in solving customers' specific legal problems (e.g. researching public and private databases for certain types of information, drafting and analyzing contractual provisions and whole documents, analyzing briefs and filings, corporate governance, conducting due diligence).
- Lead product demonstrations tailored to the context of various law firm practice groups and in-house legal teams, asking questions to validate how Harvey can add value and then showcasing Harvey's features and benefits relevant to each prospective client's potential use cases.
- Partner with the marketing team to develop content that will resonate with lawyers, tailored to the unique needs of their practice areas and client types.
- Act as the "Voice of the Customer," using your legal perspective to help the broader sales team to develop and implement more effective strategies and synthesize customer feedback for the product team through a legal lens.
- Tailor the introduction of new solutions to specific customer needs.
- Further the market perception of Harvey as uniquely credible, substantive, and helpful in applying its AI solutions to make lawyers better at their jobs.
- Conduct research and analysis on customers and competitors.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- Fluent in German and English.
- At least 3 years of experience practicing law at a top-tier law firm (Vault 50 or equivalent), preferably with a transactional, in-house or transformation experience.
- Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.
- Outstanding presentation skills to both legal and executive audiences, whether impromptu on a whiteboard or using presentations and demos.
- Strong understanding of legal processes and challenges faced by legal professionals.
- Sales or customer-facing experience, including law firm business development and/or secondment, is a plus, as is experience directly managing law firm client matters and client relationships.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR POSTINGS
- Location: Germany
- Work eligibility: Must have valid German work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

We're looking for a Lead Product Owner, Finance Systems to own the systems and workflows that power Harvey's finance organization as we scale globally.
This role sits at the center of our finance technology portfolio: NetSuite as the ERP core, Zip for procurement intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex for spend and card programs, and Metronome for usage-based billing.
You'll help shape the roadmap across that portfolio, prioritize competing demands, and drive changes from discovery through deployment, all in an agile and high-growth environment.
You'll partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Procurement, and Tax, as well as teams across Business Technology (where the Finance Systems team lives) and Security, to translate business needs into scalable, well-governed solutions.
