section_responsibilities:
- Act as the product owner for one or more of Harvey's core finance business process areas (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), along with the systems that serve them.
Run discovery with process owners, define target-state process and system design, own the roadmap, and measure success based on value add output and accuracy.
- Lead the hardest problems in your domain, where there's no established pattern to configure against.
That could be international expansion and the entity, currency, tax, and statutory complexity that comes with it, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Develop and maintain a holistic architecture strategy for the finance applications ecosystem: where each system's boundaries sit, how data moves between them, and what Harvey will need short, mid and long term.
Work with the owners of adjacent enterprise systems, including Workday and Salesforce, on the integrations and handoffs finance depends on.
- Find manual work and eliminate it, replacing spreadsheets, manual data entry, and email-based approvals with core configuration, automated workflows and integrations.
Evaluate new functionality within existing and/or new tooling for best fit at Harvey.
- Configure, maintain, and optimize NetSuite and, dependent on business process ownership determined, own the spend and revenue system workflows that feed the ledger: Zip intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex card programs and expenses, Metronome usage ingestion and downstream invoicing logic, and future tooling for advanced revenue recognition.
Understand, advise and execute on data flows, as well as the upstream product and company-wide data sources that revenue reporting depends on.
- Identify, test, and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across the processes you own in a controlled manner, with clear resulting impact of time savings and manual output eliminated.
- Own quality across your applications, ensuring lightweight SDLC to balance accuracy and agility.
Partner with leadership to set best practices and serve as the mentor and escalation point for peers across Finance and Business Technology on the portfolio's hardest design questions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 7+ years of hands-on experience as a finance systems professional, including 5+ years of direct NetSuite experience with demonstrated complex configuration depth and supporting a global, multi-entity and multi-currency finance organization.
- Product owner or product manager experience in at least one core finance business process area (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), with extensive depth in that domain: discovery with process owners, target-state process design, proposing tradeoffs or workarounds, and owning a roadmap through delivery.
Familiarity with the adjacent areas matters more than equal depth in all three.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at various levels of the business and technology organizations: adapting how you make a case depending on the audience, building alignment across cross-functional teams, and saying no to a request and explaining why.
A track record of mentoring peers, setting technical standards, or being the expert others escalate to on hard problems.
- Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, high-stakes process problems without an existing playbook, operating with a high degree of autonomy while knowing when to pull others in on high-impact decisions.
Examples include international expansion and multi-entity or multi-currency complexity, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Deep understanding of leading and emerging trends in SaaS finance applications and architecture, including where automation and AI are truly driving innovation.
- Direct experience implementing best practices around change management, regression and UAT planning, segregation of duties, and regulatory requirements, while increasing efficiencies.

We're hiring an experienced, hands-on leader to shape GTM Strategy & Operations for Harvey in APAC.
You'll join the Revenue Operations organization, which serves as the core strategic and business partner to Harvey's global GTM teams, with a mission to drive sustained, efficient growth and operational excellence.

section_responsibilities:

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
As a Product Data Scientist, you will be a core member of Harvey's product development organization and one of the foundational members of the Data Science function.
You will partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Go-to-Market, and company leadership to define how we measure product success, understand user behavior, and make high-quality decisions in a fast-moving environment.
This role is both strategic and hands-on.
You will define north-star and product-level metrics, design experiments and causal analyses, build source-of-truth reporting, and turn ambiguous product questions into clear recommendations.
You should be comfortable operating where the data is imperfect, the product is evolving quickly, and the right answer requires both analytical rigor and strong product judgment.
section_responsibilities:
- Embed with Product and Engineering teams as a trusted analytical partner, identifying opportunities to improve user experience, adoption, retention, and business impact.
- Define and maintain core metrics that create a shared understanding of product performance and customer value.
- Design and evaluate experiments, including A/B tests and causal inference methods, to measure the impact of product, model, and workflow changes.
- Analyze product usage, customer segments, and go-to-market signals to surface insights, size opportunities, and inform roadmap decisions.
- Build dashboards, reports, and self-serve tools that help teams answer product questions with confidence.
- Develop models, forecasts, and analytical frameworks to explain user behavior, detect anomalies, and guide prioritization.
- Translate complex analyses into clear recommendations for technical, business, and executive audiences.
- Partner with Engineering and Data teams to improve the infrastructure that powers analytics, experimentation, and decision-making.
- Establish the standards, practices, and culture for Product Data Science at Harvey.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, economics, statistics, or another quantitative field, ideally in a high-growth product company, AI company, research organization, or similarly ambiguous environment.
- A strong track record of using SQL, Python, and statistical methods to answer product questions and turn analysis into product or business impact.
- Experience defining new metrics and measurement frameworks from scratch, especially for products where usage patterns, customer value, or success criteria are still being discovered.
- Deep fluency in experimentation, causal inference, A/B testing, and statistical modeling, with good judgment about when precision matters and when directional clarity is enough.
- Strong product instincts and curiosity about how users adopt, evaluate, and expand their use of AI-enabled workflows.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to influence Product, Engineering, Go-to-Market, and executive stakeholders through clear reasoning and compelling data stories.
- Comfort creating structure in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and raising the quality of decision-making for the teams.
Bonus
- Experience with AI/ML products, large language models, developer tools, enterprise software, or products used in complex professional workflows.
- Experience as an early data science or analytics hire at a hyper-growth startup, including helping define team norms, tooling, and best practices.
- Experience supporting enterprise or B2B products, including analysis of adoption, engagement, retention, expansion, or go-to-market motion.
- Familiarity with modern data infrastructure and the practical tradeoffs involved in building reliable analytics in a rapidly evolving product environment.

job_title: Senior VLSI CAD and AI Automation Engineer
section_intro:
NVIDIA is at the forefront of AI-driven innovation in VLSI design automation.
Join us to shape the future of semiconductor design with cutting-edge AI tools and make a significant impact in a collaborative, high-performance environment.
Are you ready to push the boundaries of what's possible in VLSI CAD?
Come be part of our pioneering team!
section_responsibilities:
You will be responsible for developing and integrating advanced CAD solutions and automation flows using AI and machine learning for VLSI design, verification, and implementation.
Work closely with design, verification, and CAD teams to identify areas for improving VLSI workflows using advanced tools and methods.
Research, prototype, and deploy AI-based algorithms.
Develop and maintain scripts and automation infrastructure to enable seamless adoption of AI tools in the VLSI design process.
Continuously review emerging AI technologies and methodologies to keep our CAD environment up-to-date.
Provide technical support and training to engineering teams on AI-enabled CAD flows and best practices.
section_requirements:
B.Sc./M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of experience in VLSI CAD tool development, with a strong focus on integrating AI/ML techniques into EDA workflows.
Proficiency in Python and at least one AI/ML framework (such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or scikit-learn).
Hands-on experience with VLSI physical design and familiarity with industry-standard EDA tools (e.g., Synopsys, Cadence).
Knowledge of data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model deployment as applied to VLSI design challenges.
Experience developing and maintaining automation scripts (Python, Perl, Tcl, Make).
Strong analytical skills in evaluating the impact of AI solutions on design quality, performance, and productivity.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced environment.
Self-motivation, attention to detail, and a track record of delivering robust solutions to production.
section_preferred:
Demonstrated experience deploying AI/ML models in production VLSI CAD environments.
Contributions to open-source AI/EDA projects or publications in relevant conferences/journals.
Deep understanding of VLSI design challenges-such as timing closure, power optimization, or yield enhancement-and how AI can address them.
Experience with cloud-based or distributed compute environments for large-scale AI training and inference.
Strong ownership, curiosity, and a passion for continuous learning and innovation.

OpenAI's Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems.
We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.
We are looking for customer-focused software engineers to build effective custom software that leverages OpenAI's APIs to solve real customer problems.
As an FDSWE, you will work with our customers and OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers to design and implement scalable solutions that solve their most difficult problems.
You will design abstractions to solve customer problems, and then use them to scale our speed and quality of delivery across all Forward Deployed engagements.
You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architects, and Customer Success Managers who work on the same account.
You will also work with our Research and Applied Product and Engineering teams to provide insightful customer feedback.
This role is based in San Francisco.
Travel up to 50% is required.
section_responsibilities:
- Embed deeply with strategic customers to understand their business challenges and technical requirements in detail.
- Design, architect, and develop full-stack solutions using an experiment-driven, iterative approach.
- Prepare detailed scopes of work and project plans for both proof-of-concept prototypes and full production deployments.
- Work hands-on with customers' technical teams as a technical expert and trusted advisor, coding side-by-side to drive projects to completion on their infrastructure.
- Collaborate with Product, Research and Applied teams to ensure seamless customer experiences, project success and actionable product feedback
- Contribute to internal knowledge bases, codifying best practices and sharing insights gained from customer engagements to scale the Forward Deployed Engineering function.
section_requirements:

- Former founder, or early engineer at a startup who has built a product from scratch is a plus
- Experience with relational databases like Postgres/MySQL
- Have a bias for action and willingness to work iteratively with your customers to deliver the right solution that solves their problem.

section_about:
OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems.
We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.
Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.
As an Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes.
You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.
You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness.
Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact-not simply activity or successful demonstrations.
This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI's products evolve.
This role is based in our SF or NYC office.
section_responsibilities:
- Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.
- Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.
- Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.
- Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.
- Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.
- Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.
- Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.
section_requirements:
- Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production.
Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.
- Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering-not only program or stakeholder management.
- Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
- Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.
- Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
- Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
- Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.
- Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.
- Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems.
The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.
The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.
We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and integrate power-generation and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses.
You will work across prime movers, fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, water treatment, heat recovery, acoustics, fire interfaces, and plant auxiliaries.
The role combines first-principles engineering with practical vendor and field execution to deliver systems that are safe, efficient, maintainable, and ready for demanding operating profiles.
Travel: 50%
section_responsibilities:
- Develop mechanical basis-of-design documents, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, specifications, calculations, and equipment requirements for power generation facilities.
- Design and review prime-mover auxiliaries, fuel gas or liquid fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, lubrication, compressed air, water treatment, and heat-recovery systems.
- Evaluate thermal performance, hydraulic behavior, pressure drop, vibration, acoustics, emissions interfaces, redundancy, and maintenance requirements.
- Translate generation duty cycles and data center load profiles into equipment sizing, operating envelopes, and control requirements.
- Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment selections, test plans, failure modes, service strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.
- Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.
- Coordinate interfaces with electrical, controls, CSA, fuel supply, environmental, fire protection, and data center mechanical teams.
- Create repeatable mechanical reference designs and standards for future generation deployments.
section_requirements:
- 8+ years of mechanical engineering experience on power generation, oil and gas, industrial utilities, central plants, or mission-critical projects.
- Strong knowledge of rotating equipment, piping, heat transfer, fluid systems, thermal performance, ventilation, and mechanical auxiliaries.
- Experience with combined heat and power, heat recovery, modular generation, or microgrids.
- Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, generators, or comparable large industrial equipment.
- Ability to evaluate vendor data, equipment curves, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance constraints.
- Experience carrying designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and performance validation.
- Knowledge of applicable ASME, API, NFPA, ASHRAE, and environmental requirements.
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.
section_preferred:
- Professional Engineer license.
- Experience with process simulation, hydraulic modeling, CFD, or equipment-performance modeling.
- Experience supporting high-density data center loads and rapid infrastructure deployment.

job_title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer - Foundations, Search
section_about:
The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI.
Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models.
Pushing the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, and efficiency improvements to propel our science.
The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack (serving, indexing, retrieval) to translate model intent into reliable, real-world actions.
Operating at the frontier of AI and information retrieval, the team develops large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to reason over global knowledge and act dependably.
In close partnership with researchers, we rapidly bring modeling breakthroughs into production and redefine how intelligent systems discover, retrieve, and synthesize information at planetary scale.
We're looking for a researcher focused on our search efforts.
You'll work with a a team of world-class research scientists and engineers developing foundational technology that enables models to retrieve and condition on the right information, at the right time.
This includes designing new embedding training objectives, scalable vector store architectures, and dynamic indexing methods.
This work will support retrieval across many OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication and deep technical impact.
section_responsibilities:
- Tackle embedding models and retrieval systems optimized for grounding, relevance, and adaptive reasoning.
- Collaborate with a team of researchers and engineers building end-to-end infrastructure for training, evaluating, and integrating embeddings into frontier models.
- Drive innovation in dense, sparse, and hybrid representation techniques, metric learning, and learning-to-retrieve systems.
- Collaborate closely with Pretraining, Inference, and other Research teams to integrate retrieval throughout the model lifecycle
- Contribute to OpenAI's long-term vision of AI systems with memory and knowledge access capabilities rooted in learned representations.
section_requirements:
- Proven experience leading high-performance teams of researchers or engineers in ML infrastructure or foundational research.
- Deep technical expertise in representation learning, embedding models, or vector retrieval systems.
- Familiarity with transformer-based LLMs and how embedding spaces can interact with language model objectives.
- Research experience in areas such as contrastive learning, supervised or unsupervised embedding learning, or metric learning.
- A track record of building or scaling large machine learning systems, particularly embedding pipelines in production or research contexts.
- A first-principles mindset for challenging assumptions about how retrieval and memory should work for large models.

section_about:
Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI's API platform.
These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world.
We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for.
Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.
We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering.
These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.
That reach creates challenging engineering problems.
We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change.
The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.
Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for.
The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.
We're hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience.
Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.
- Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.
- Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.
- Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.
- Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.
- Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.
- Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.
- Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.
- Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.
section_preferred:
- Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.
- Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.
- Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

section_about:
The Applied AI Engineering (Codex) team helps customers adopt OpenAI's coding tools throughout their software development lifecycle.
We act as trusted technical partners, guiding engineering teams as they integrate Codex into their projects and workflows.
Our customers span digital-native companies to global enterprises, and we work side-by-side to accelerate how they plan, build, and deliver software.
We are seeking a technically deep, creativity-driven Applied AI Engineer who is already a power user of AI coding tools and passionate about pushing the boundaries of developer productivity.
You will partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on builders to design, validate, and scale advanced AI workflows, often using Codex to prototype and build the very demos, integrations, and automations customers ultimately adopt.
This is a highly cross-functional role that blends technical architecture, product strategy, and customer-facing leadership.
You'll work closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Applied Engineering, and the broader Codex organization to advocate for customer needs, shape product direction, and accelerate the successful deployment of intelligent coding systems across some of the world's most influential companies.
This role is based in Singapore.
section_responsibilities:
- Serve as the primary technical subject matter expert on OpenAI Codex for a portfolio of customers, embedding deeply with them to enable their engineering teams and build coding workflows.
- Partner directly with customers to design and implement AI-enhanced development workflows, from rapid prototyping through scalable production rollout.
- Build high-quality demos, reference implementations, and workflow automations, using Codex itself as part of your development process.
- Lead large-format workshops, technical deep dives, and hands-on enablement sessions that help engineering organizations adopt AI coding tools effectively and safely.
- Contribute technical content including examples, guides, patterns, and best practices to the OpenAI Cookbook to help the broader developer community accelerate their work with Codex.
- Gather high-fidelity product insights from real customer deployments and translate them into clear product proposals and model feedback for internal teams.
- Influence customer strategy and decision-making by framing how AI coding tools fit into their SDLC, technical roadmap, and organizational workflows.
- Serve as a trusted advisor on solution architecture, operational readiness, model configuration, security considerations, and best-practice adoption.
section_requirements:
- Ability to speak Mandarin is a requirement as you will be working with Mandarin-speaking customers and/or vendors in the role.
- Have 5+ years of technical consulting, post-sales engineering, solutions architecture, or similar experience working directly with customers.
- Are an active power user of AI coding tools and have deeply customized your own developer workflow; you have a point of view on what makes engineers more productive.
- Enjoy building scrappy, high-signal demos, integrations, and prototypes that clearly articulate what Codex can enable, often using Codex to accelerate your own development process.
- Have experience delivering large, high-impact workshops or technical training to engineering teams and know how to craft sessions that are engaging, hands-on, and outcomes-driven.
- Have contributed technical guides, patterns, or examples publicly and care about clarity, pedagogy, and community impact.
- Communicate complex technical concepts in clear, persuasive written and verbal form especially when helping customers make strategic decisions about where and how to apply AI.
- Are excited by ambiguous, rapidly evolving problem spaces and enjoy iterating toward novel solutions hand-in-hand with customers.
- Care about customer success, reliability, safety, and operational excellence as much as you care about technical ingenuity.

section_about:
Security is at the foundation of OpenAI's mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
The Security team protects OpenAI's technology, people, and products.
We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI.
Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.
As a Security Engineer, Application Security you will be responsible for identifying and mitigating security vulnerabilities within software applications through building security tools, code reviews, penetration testing, and security assessments.
We're looking for people who will work closely with development teams to ensure secure coding practices are integrated throughout the software development lifecycle, preventing security risks before they emerge.
You will also provide security guidance to developers and other stakeholders, fostering a culture of security awareness within the organization.
The role is preferred to be based in San Francisco, Seattle or New York City but may consider remote work.
section_responsibilities:
- Perform Security Assessments: Conduct regular security assessments, code reviews, and penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities in applications and software.
- Develop and Implement Security Tools: Design, develop, and implement security tools, frameworks, and methodologies to protect applications against security threats.
- Collaborate with Development Teams: Work closely with development teams to ensure security best practices are integrated throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including secure coding guidelines.
- Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment: Conduct threat modeling and risk assessments to proactively identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies.
- Vulnerability Management: Track, analyze, and manage vulnerabilities in applications, providing guidance and support for remediation efforts.
- Incident Response Support: Assist in investigating, analyzing, and responding to security incidents related to applications, ensuring timely resolution and documentation of incidents.
- Stay Current on Security Trends: Continuously stay updated on the latest security threats, vulnerabilities, and technologies to enhance security measures in applications.
section_requirements:
- Extensive experience in information security, cybersecurity, or a related field, with a significant portion of that experience in leadership or management roles.
- Deep understanding of security technologies, tools, and best practices, including experience with secure coding practices, threat modeling, risk assessments, and incident response.
- Experience in application security, software development, or related areas with a strong understanding of secure coding practices and application security frameworks.
- Proficiency in programming languages (such as Python, Java, C++, etc.), knowledge of security tools (e.g., Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP), and familiarity with security protocols and encryption methods.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex security issues to both technical and non-technical audiences

section_about:
Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings.
Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors.
We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples' lives.
As a Test Engineer on the Robotics team, you will help shape the next generation of embodied AI.
You'll design and run rigorous, exploratory and requirements-driven tests-building custom test equipment, analyzing results, and translating findings into actionable insights that drive design breakthroughs and mitigate risks across hardware and software.
This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how our AI scales beyond simulation, ensuring that every design, test, and iteration brings us closer to truly adaptive, versatile robotic systems.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and build custom test benches to evaluate system performance under realistic operating conditions; proficient in CAD and familiar with GD&T.
- Analyze and interpret test data to identify trends, anomalies, and root causes.
- Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans that validate mechanical performance against product requirements.
- Execute validation and verification testing, capturing both quantitative and qualitative data with high fidelity.
- Author clear, actionable test reports that summarize results, highlight risks, and recommend design or process changes.
- Partner with engineering, product, and leadership teams to inform design iterations and strategic decisions.
- Design and execute compliance and regulatory testing campaigns, informing in-house vs 3rd party testing strategy
section_requirements:
- Have strong intuition for mechanical and electromechanical systems and how they fail, degrade, or vary in real-world operation.
- Enjoy hands-on lab work designing, instrumenting, operating, and debugging test equipment and robotic hardware.
- Can turn evolving requirements and ambiguous failures into repeatable tests, trustworthy data, and clear engineering decisions.
- Balance rigorous validation, safety, and traceability with rapid hardware iteration.
- Communicate clearly across mechanical, electrical, software, controls, and manufacturing teams, and build alignment on risks and corrective actions.
section_preferred:
- 7+ years of experience in hardware testing or validation, including at least 2 years working with robotics hardware components and systems.
- Bachelor's or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- Experience designing test fixtures and stands using CAD, engineering drawings, and GD&T.
- Hands-on experience integrating sensors, instrumentation, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems, including calibration and measurement traceability.
- Experience developing automated or hardware-in-the-loop tests using Python, C/C++, or AI coding tools for test execution, data collection, and analysis.
- Experience designing reliability, accelerated life, environmental, and hardware qualification tests for robotic or electromechanical systems.
- Experience supporting EVT, DVT, PVT, pilot production, or sustaining hardware validation.
- Experience using root cause analysis, FMEA, or FEA to guide design improvements.
- Experience executing product standards compliance certification campaigns.

OpenAI's Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads.

We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

section_about:
Strategic Sourcing & Procurement helps OpenAI secure the products, services, and partnerships that support our research, build our products, and grow our business.
We work with teams across the company to make sound commercial decisions and move important work forward.
As OpenAI grows, we are rethinking how sourcing works: bringing expertise into decisions earlier, simplifying contracting, and using AI to give Procurement more time for judgment and strategic work.
What we learn internally-and through our supplier and enterprise-buyer relationships-can also inform better products, partnerships, and industry adoption.
We're looking for a senior leader to head Sourcing Enablement & Delivery, leading sourcing operational delivery, contracting enablement, and AI transformation-and building Procurement's contribution to OpenAI's commercial growth.
You will build the teams, systems, service model, and cross-functional partnerships that enable sourcing and contracting at scale, helping teams move quickly without losing commercial discipline or accountability.
You will partner with GTM, Sales, and Partnerships to develop Procurement's contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth.
Bring procurement-industry knowledge, buyer insights, and lessons from internal AI use into customer engagement, product feedback, and opportunities across the procurement ecosystem.
Reporting to the Head of Strategic Sourcing, you will manage the Sourcing Delivery and Contract Management leaders and shape this new function's priorities, team, and measures of success.
PRIORITIES AND WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
- A focused roadmap: clear choices about what to build first, what to defer, and how progress will be measured.
- Stronger delivery: capable leaders and teams, faster execution, less rework, and fewer unresolved ownership gaps.
- AI adoption: sustained use of AI-enabled capabilities, with measurable gains in quality, capacity, and user experience.
- Commercial results: increased OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry and a measurable contribution to commercial growth, consistent with independent supplier selection and purchasing decisions.
section_responsibilities:
- Build and lead the organization.
Hire and develop managers, coach performance, and build succession and leadership depth.
Decide how employees, contractors, delivery partners, and AI share the work.
Hold leaders accountable for results, capacity, and team health.
- Own sourcing enablement and delivery operations.
Set service commitments and quality standards with the Delivery and Contract Management leaders.
Match support to deal complexity and risk, and use internal customer feedback to improve the service.
Category and Sourcing leads retain ownership of their strategies and deals, including supplier selection, negotiations, and purchasing.
- Lead the sourcing operating rhythm.
Bring demand, priorities, and capacity into one forward plan, informed by workload and performance data.
Work with category leaders to make tradeoffs, resolve dependencies, and follow through on commitments.
Provide inputs to Procurement-wide planning and functional business reviews.
- Strengthen contracting.
Partner with Legal and Procurement Operations/COE on contract lifecycle management, approved templates, and negotiation playbooks that improve quality and free category teams to focus on strategic deals.
- Lead RACI development.
Define responsibilities, decision rights, handoffs, and escalation paths within Procurement and across partner teams.
Define how the team prioritizes work, allocates resources, and resolves delivery issues.
- Create mechanisms to bring sourcing into decisions earlier: connect business demand, supplier activity, and renewals-including work outside formal intake-with Sourcing teams, so options can be shaped before commitments and Finance and cross-functional teams can have better visibility.
- Build and prove AI-enabled ways of working.
Own use-case priorities, adoption, and business outcomes for sourcing and contracting experiences that begin in ChatGPT and connect to trusted enterprise systems.
Partner with Finance Enterprise Technology on technical delivery and with Legal, Security, and Operations on controls and support, including preserving access restrictions and contractual commitments.
Turn what works into reusable capabilities, demonstrations, and product feedback.
- Define Procurement's commercial-enablement approach with GTM, Partnerships, Legal, and Compliance including program scope, decision rights, purchasing independence, and information-sharing boundaries.
Lead Procurement's analysis, coordination, and follow-through for approved programs; GTM owns customer sales.
Maintain independent purchasing decision-making and identify and escalate any proposed linkage between OpenAI's purchasing commitments and customer sales.
- Help define goals and measures of success for Procurement's contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth with Sourcing leadership and cross-functional partners.
- Bring procurement-buyer expertise into GTM.
Own this team's buyer insights and use cases.
Work with Marketing, Sales, Product, Customer Success, and Partnerships to shape demonstrations, industry content, and customer conversations, using examples approved for external use.
- Drive OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry.
Work with Sourcing leadership, partners and GTM to explore how Procurement third-parties and partners can adopt and distribute OpenAI capabilities.
Contribute industry expertise and evidence from internal use; GTM and Partnerships own commercialization.
- Partner with Legal and Compliance to embed business-integrity and confidentiality safeguards; implement required disclosures, recusals, and independent-decision making arrangements.
section_requirements:
- Have 12+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or commercial leadership, with strong judgment about supplier choices, negotiations, contracts, and risk.
- Have built or transformed a procurement capability through rapid growth or change, with clear evidence of better execution, commercial outcomes, or user experience.
- Have managed managers and developed strong teams through hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and thoughtful use of internal and external capacity.
- Have worked in or closely with marketing, sales, or commercial teams, ideally serving procurement buyers.
You can turn customer needs into use cases and business cases, and deliver commercial results with partner teams.
- Know the procurement industry-its buyers, technology providers, service firms, and buying priorities.
You understand how to sell to Procurement, including how buyers assess risk, negotiate, and secure internal support.
- Use industry analysts, market research, buyer conversations, and professional networks to form a point of view on emerging trends and inform roadmaps, partnerships, and GTM priorities.
- Have turned AI, automation, or enterprise technology into capabilities people use.
You can work with technical partners, drive adoption, measure improvements, and recognize where human judgment remains essential.
- Can set direction when the path is not defined.
You prioritize work and resources, explain tradeoffs plainly, and earn support from teams you do not manage.
You are curious about AI and willing to test, learn, and change course.

section_about:
OpenAI's mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
GTM Systems builds and operates the tools that help our teams serve customers.
We turn operational needs into reliable workflows, integrations, and automation so support teams can focus on helping customers.
We're looking for a highly autonomous systems engineer to own and improve the systems that support our government work, including Salesforce and related integrations.
Government systems will be your primary focus, with opportunities to contribute to other priorities.
You'll build the platforms and workflows our support teams rely on, including Salesforce Service Cloud.
The work spans new capabilities, ongoing maintenance, automation, and reliability.
You'll identify needs, clarify scope, make technical decisions, and carry work through implementation, testing, production validation, and ongoing operation.
You'll work closely with government, support, operations, Security, and engineering partners to understand constraints and deliver systems that work well in practice.
section_responsibilities:
- Own government support systems from problem definition through design, delivery, production validation, and ongoing operation.
Turn ambiguous needs into clear priorities and practical technical plans.
- Design and build maintainable service workflows, data models, interfaces, and integrations.
- Partner with government, support, operations, security, and engineering teams to make technical tradeoffs and translate access, data-handling, and change-control requirements into working solutions.
- Improve reliability and performance through automated tests, observability, safe releases, incident response, and recovery.
Validate changes in production and address recurring failure modes.
- Document architecture, operational procedures, and recovery paths so systems are understandable and supportable.
Automate repetitive work and contribute to other GASS priorities as needed.
section_requirements:
- Prior experience delivering or operating systems in a government environment is required.
You can explain how operational, access, or change-control constraints shaped your engineering decisions.
- Deep Salesforce Service Cloud experience, including Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, data modeling, configuration, and integrations.
Sound judgment about when to use code or declarative automation.
- A track record of owning ambiguous technical work independently: identifying needs, defining scope, coordinating partners, making decisions, and following through after launch.
- Strong software engineering fundamentals: clear architecture, readable code, automated tests, and familiarity with languages such as Python or Java.
- Experience with Salesforce security and permissions, appropriate data handling, production reliability, incident response, and recovery.
- A strong understanding of support workflows and the ability to translate operational needs into maintainable systems.
Clear communication and sound judgment about when to involve partners or escalate a decision.
- Preferred: relevant Salesforce certifications, such as Platform Developer II, Service Cloud Consultant, Platform App Builder, or Application Architect.
- Preferred: experience applying AI or automation to support operations.
Candidates must be eligible and willing to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
An active clearance is not required at the time of hire, and OpenAI will sponsor the clearance process.

section_about:
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own actuator development and integration from system goals through production readiness.
The actuator program spans mechanical, electrical, firmware, harnessing, controls, test, reliability, manufacturing, and supply chain, and needs a TPM who can turn cross-functional decisions into clear scope, executable milestones, and timely decisions.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.
section_responsibilities:
- Drive actuator programs end-to-end, aligning scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria across engineering teams.
- Drive scope lock and technical convergence for sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals while connecting component decisions to system performance.
- Coordinate actuator development across motors, gears, sensing, electronics, and firmware, and align the electrical and mechanical interfaces that connect actuators to the broader robot.
- Lead validation planning from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.
- Drive tradeoff decisions across cost, quality, performance, schedule, and lead time by collaborating cross-functionally and quantifying impact to meet program deliverables.
- Establish effective mechanisms for technical reviews, change control, design releases, decision tracking, and manufacturing readiness.
- Surface risks early and drive decisions, owners, and actions to closure.
- Cross-functional scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria are aligned across engineering, supply chain and manufacturing teams.
- Sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals converge on decisions connected to system performance.
- Validation is planned from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.
- Risks, tradeoffs, owners, and actions are surfaced early and driven to closure to meet program deliverables.
- Mitigation strategies are well communicated and aligned upon, acceleration of hardware development from design to trials on the floor is quantifiable.
- Tools and workflows built are well embedded in the daily routine of all the team members, thus do not seem an added overhead to get things done.
section_requirements:
- Have led complex electromechanical hardware programs from development through manufacturing.
- Are equally comfortable reasoning about an actuator's internal architecture and how it integrates into the larger system through PCBAs, connectors, cables,etc.
- Can work effectively across ME, EE, firmware, interconnecting harnesses, controls, test, reliability, manufacturing, and supply chain.
- Understand hardware development realities including prototype cycles, long-lead parts, suppliers, testing, design changes, and production ramp.

section_about:
The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact.
We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption.
The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.
Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners-including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners-to extend OpenAI's technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers.

You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from AI opportunity and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.
You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions.
In close partnership with the Revenue Partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities.
You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements-leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins-while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale.
You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed.
The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations.
section_responsibilities:
- Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a portfolio of strategic partners, building trusted relationships with their executives, AI leaders, architects, engineering teams, and delivery organizations.
- Partner closely with the Revenue Partnerships team as one virtual team, aligning partner strategy, technical priorities, joint customer opportunities, and measures of success.
- Develop the technical strategy and plan for each partner, identifying priority solutions, use cases, technical capabilities, enablement needs, delivery risks, and opportunities to drive customer adoption.
- Assess prospective and existing partners' technical capabilities and delivery readiness, identifying strengths, gaps, and the investments required to successfully deliver OpenAI-powered solutions.
- Lead technical discovery with partners and joint customers to identify, qualify, and prioritize AI use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.
- Develop clear Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.
- Collaborate with partner sales and technical teams on strategic opportunities, providing technical guidance through discovery, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, architectural recommendations, and proofs of value.
- Guide partners through their initial and most strategic OpenAI deployments, helping them navigate technical tradeoffs and production dependencies while ensuring solutions meet a high bar for quality, security, reliability, and responsible deployment.
- Build partner capability and technical self-sufficiency through tailored enablement, architectural guidance, reusable solution patterns, technical workshops, and mentorship.
- Establish clear standards and mechanisms for partner-delivered solution quality, identifying risks early and intervening when architecture, implementation, security, evaluation, or adoption issues threaten customer outcomes.
- Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams.
- Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed.
- Identify repeatable patterns across partner engagements and turn them into architectures, playbooks, reference solutions, and best practices that allow successful approaches to scale across partners and customers.
- Bring insights from partners and joint customers back to Product, Engineering, Research, and Partnerships, helping shape product strategy, technical guidance, and the broader OpenAI partner ecosystem.
section_requirements:
- Have significant experience in senior customer- or partner-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, partner engineering, field architecture, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical consulting.
- Have worked successfully with global or regional system integrators, consulting firms, or other technology partners, and understand how partner organizations sell, architect, and deliver complex enterprise technology.
- Have guided complex enterprise organizations from technical discovery and evaluation through production deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.
- Can build credibility with CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, partner executives, and AI leaders while communicating equally effectively with architects and hands-on engineers.
- Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, and governance.
- Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLMs, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, and enterprise AI workflows.
- Can prototype when useful, explain technical tradeoffs clearly, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.
- Have experience enabling technical organizations at scale, turning your own expertise into repeatable architectures, training, patterns, and practices that others can successfully apply.
- Understand enterprise security and compliance requirements and can guide partners and customers through the technical considerations required to move AI systems safely into production.
- Are comfortable balancing the needs of OpenAI, the partner, and the end customer, and can exercise sound judgment when those priorities do not perfectly align.
- Know when to go deep personally, when to coach a partner toward the answer, and when to engage specialist resources.
- Can prioritize across a portfolio of partners and customer opportunities, focusing technical resources on the work most likely to create durable customer value and adoption.
- Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity into a practical architecture, executive decision, enablement plan, or path to production.
- Own problems end-to-end, learn quickly, and care deeply about helping partners and customers deploy advanced AI responsibly.

OpenAI's Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) team partners across the company to enable safe, responsible growth.
This role will be a senior EHS partner to our robotics operations as our operating footprint expands.
You will work closely with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and external partners to integrate safety into how our facilities are designed, built, staffed, and operated.
We are seeking a Senior Manager, EHS - Robotics to provide senior, hands-on safety leadership across multiple sites.
This role is for an experienced EHS leader who can operate independently in a fast-moving technical environment, anticipate risk before it becomes an incident, and build practical safety systems that scale with the business.
Our robotics operations are scaling quickly, with a growing mix of construction, commissioning, workforce expansion, and around-the-clock operations.
This creates a complex and evolving risk environment and requires strong preventive planning, consistent field presence, and sustained incident-management oversight.
This leader will own site-level EHS strategy and execution for the robotics portfolio while partnering with the broader EHS team on company-wide standards and programs.
The successful candidate will look around corners: planning for future ramps, identifying requirements early, influencing design and operating decisions, and creating durable systems that enable teams to move quickly without compromising safety.
section_responsibilities:
- Serve as a senior EHS partner across robotics R&D operations, owning site-level safety strategy, priorities, and execution as the footprint scales.
- Anticipate EHS requirements for new operations, equipment, processes, construction phases, staffing ramps, and 24/7 operations, and translate them into practical plans before work begins.
- Lead proactive risk identification and control across robotics activities, including machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and other site-specific risks.
- Build and maintain site EHS programs, risk assessments, procedures, training, inspections, corrective-action systems, emergency preparedness, and compliance processes appropriate to each site's risk profile.
- Partner with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and vendors to embed safety into facility design, equipment deployment, work planning, and operating decisions.
- Provide visible field leadership across shifts and operating conditions, establishing mechanisms that support effective EHS coverage and escalation for 24/7 operations.
- Lead incident response and investigation for significant events; ensure timely fact-finding, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, verification, trend analysis, and communication of lessons learned.
- Use incident, near-miss, inspection, and operational data to identify recurring risks and drive preventive actions across sites rather than addressing events in isolation.
- Oversee contractor and contingent-worker safety interfaces, clarifying responsibilities, expectations, reporting, and corrective-action ownership across multi-employer worksites.
- Maintain strong regulatory compliance and readiness, including applicable Cal/OSHA and OSHA requirements, while developing metrics and reporting that make site risks, actions, and performance visible to leadership.
section_requirements:
- 15+ years of progressive EHS experience, including significant leadership responsibility in robotics, advanced manufacturing, R&D, industrial, or similarly complex technical environments.
- Strong technical knowledge across occupational safety and health, with depth in areas such as machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, hazardous energy, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and incident investigation.
- Demonstrated experience supporting complex sites through rapid scale, construction and operational overlap, commissioning, process change, or transition to extended or 24/7 operations.
- Strong working knowledge of OSHA and Cal/OSHA requirements and the ability to translate regulatory obligations into practical, scalable operating programs.
- Demonstrated success influencing senior technical and operational leaders, especially where EHS does not directly own the work and decisions must be made through partnership.
- Experience building EHS systems, programs, metrics, vendor support, and operating rhythms for an emerging or rapidly scaling organization.
- Strong judgment and the ability to balance operational speed, technical complexity, workforce needs, compliance, and risk without defaulting to overly rigid solutions.
- Clear, credible communication skills with executives, engineers, operators, contractors, employees, and external partners, including the ability to communicate during high-pressure incidents.
- Comfort operating independently in ambiguity, with the technical depth, field orientation, pragmatism, and ownership needed to anticipate what is coming and build durable safety capability ahead of growth.

job_title: Full Stack Software Engineer - Codex for Finance
section_about:
OpenAI for Financial Services is part of OpenAI's Verticals organization, which focuses on accelerating the economy and knowledge work.
We build AI products for financial institutions and the professionals who power them, from investment bankers and research analysts to investors and other financial services teams.
We combine OpenAI's models, financial data, and enterprise knowledge to help professionals research companies, analyze markets, and produce high-quality work in the tools they use every day.
We're a small, entrepreneurial team working closely with customers and partners across research, product, design, engineering, and go-to-market to bring new capabilities from idea to production.
We're looking for full-stack engineers to build new, AI-native products on top of ChatGPT Work and Codex.
This is zero-to-one work: you'll help define how financial professionals research, analyze, and make decisions alongside AI.
You'll own the experience across the stack, work directly with customers to understand their workflows, and collaborate across OpenAI to turn new model capabilities into products that professionals can trust.
Your work will shape how some of the world's largest financial institutions adopt AI and how financial knowledge work gets done.
section_responsibilities:
- Build a new financial services app within ChatGPT Work and Codex, creating intuitive AI-native experiences for company research, financial analysis, document review, and professional work products.
- Develop new product experiences around enterprise memory that learn from an organization's knowledge, workflows, and context, and adapt to how its teams work.
- Develop the APIs, services, and integrations required to connect user experiences with financial data providers, enterprise systems, and OpenAI's models.
- Work closely with product and design to turn ambiguous customer problems into polished, useful, and reliable products.
- Work directly with financial institutions to understand customer needs, unblock deployments, and turn feedback into meaningful product improvements.
- Partner with research, security, infrastructure, and other engineering teams to take new capabilities from early prototype to scaled production.
section_requirements:
- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a strong track record of building and shipping production software across the stack.
- Expertise in TypeScript, React, and modern web technologies, along with strong experience building backend services in languages such as Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript.
- Experience designing and building complex product interfaces, APIs, and integrations that work together as a cohesive user experience.
- Strong product instincts and the ability to move from an ambiguous customer problem to a practical, well-engineered solution.
- Comfort working across the stack and organizational boundaries when that is what it takes to ship a great product.
- A high bar for usability, reliability, security, and performance, particularly in enterprise or other high-trust environments.
- Interest in AI and how model capabilities can be applied to complex professional work; direct AI/ML or financial services experience is helpful but not required.
- Experience as a founder, an early engineer at a startup, or an engineer who has helped build a new product from scratch is a plus.

section_about:
The Technical Success team helps OpenAI's customers realize meaningful and sustained value from our technology.
We partner with customers throughout their journey-from initial exploration and solution design to production implementation and organization-wide adoption.
Applied AI Engineers serve as trusted technical partners to customer executives, engineering teams, product leaders, security organizations, and transformation teams.
They combine deep technical judgment with strong customer instincts, translating frontier AI capabilities into secure, reliable systems and durable business outcomes.
We are seeking a Manager to build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting our enterprise customers.
You will be accountable for the technical success of a broad and strategically important customer portfolio.
You will help your team identify high-value opportunities, design and deploy production-grade AI systems, navigate complex technical and organizational constraints, and expand successful implementations across workflows, teams, and business units.
This role requires technical depth, people leadership, customer judgment, and operational rigor.
You should be comfortable coaching engineers through architecture and evaluation decisions, engaging directly in high-stakes customer situations, and collaborating with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Legal.
You will also help define how we serve enterprise customers at scale by developing effective coverage models, reusable implementation patterns, technical enablement, escalation mechanisms, and systems for turning field insights into high-quality product feedback.
section_responsibilities:
- Build, manage, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting large and complex enterprise customers.
- Own the quality and impact of the team's work across solution design, implementation, production readiness, adoption, and expansion.
- Coach the team through decisions involving architecture, model selection, evaluations, reliability, latency, safety, security, governance, and cost.
- Establish an operating model for prioritizing accounts and engagements according to customer needs, strategic value, technical complexity, and potential for repeatable impact.
- Serve as a senior technical escalation point during critical launches, production incidents, complex integrations, and high-stakes customer decisions.
- Partner with customer executives and technical leaders to connect implementation decisions to measurable business and operational outcomes.
- Help customers progress from experimentation to production systems and sustained adoption across their organizations.
- Partner closely with Sales and Solutions Engineering to create continuity throughout the customer lifecycle and maintain shared accountability for customer success.
- Translate customer needs and recurring implementation challenges into actionable feedback for Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and other internal teams.
- Identify scalable market patterns, distinguish them from bespoke requests, and advocate for investments that can benefit multiple customers.
- Develop reusable architectures, evaluation methods, playbooks, tooling, and enablement that improve time to value across the enterprise portfolio.
- Establish mechanisms for measuring production implementations, adoption, customer outcomes, delivery quality, team capacity, and the impact of reusable work.
- Hire thoughtfully, raise the technical and leadership bar, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning.
- Represent OpenAI with credibility and sound judgment in conversations with senior customer and internal stakeholders.
section_requirements:
- Have significant experience managing customer-facing technical teams, such as Applied AI Engineers, Solutions Architects, Forward Deployed Engineers, Customer Engineers, or Technical Account Managers.
- Have built or led teams responsible for implementing complex software, data, machine learning, or AI systems in enterprise environments.
- Maintain sufficient technical depth to evaluate architectures, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions, and coach engineers through difficult implementation decisions.
- Have experience taking AI, machine learning, or other technically complex systems from prototype to production.
- Understand production-system requirements, including reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, evaluation, and operational readiness.
- Have led teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, escalations, and rapidly evolving products or markets.
- Can translate effectively among technical details, customer needs, product strategy, and business outcomes.
- Have worked with large organizations involving multiple business units, stakeholder groups, procurement processes, or governance requirements.
- Demonstrate strong executive presence and can build trust with engineering leaders, business executives, security teams, and other senior stakeholders.
- Have designed operating models, coverage strategies, prioritization frameworks, or repeatable delivery processes for a growing technical organization.
- Are a strong cross-functional partner who can navigate disagreement directly while maintaining trust and shared accountability.
- Use data and clear principles to allocate limited resources across a large portfolio of opportunities.
- Care deeply about developing people and have a track record of coaching team members, raising performance, and building inclusive teams.
- Are energized by helping organizations adopt frontier AI responsibly and turn emerging capabilities into durable value.
RELEVANT EXPERIENCE MAY INCLUDE
- Leading teams in applied AI engineering, solutions architecture, forward-deployed engineering, professional services, technical consulting, or customer engineering.
- Implementing generative AI, machine learning, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, data platforms, or other complex enterprise technologies.
- Working with customers in semiconductors, media, entertainment, or similarly complex and technology-intensive industries.
- Supporting global customers, multi-business-unit implementations, regulated workflows, or large-scale organizational transformations.
- Building technical enablement, reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, or customer implementation methodologies.
Direct experience in these industries is not required.
We value leaders who can recognize common technical and organizational patterns while adapting their approach to different customer environments.

section_about:
Our Inference team brings OpenAI's most capable research and technology to the world through our products.
We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they've never been able to before.
We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.
We're looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI's state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs.
You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.
You'll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation.
We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.
section_responsibilities:
- Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.
- Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.
- Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.
- Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.
- Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.
- Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.
section_requirements:
- Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.
- Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.
- Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.
- Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.
- Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.
- Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.
- Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.
